Description:
The acquire to dispose process is a critical business process that involves
managing the lifecycle of both owned and leased assets from acquisition to
disposal. This process includes the acquisition, deployment, maintenance, and
eventual disposal of assets such as equipment, vehicles, and property. Dynamics
365 can be used to support this process by providing a centralized platform for
managing asset data, tracking asset usage and maintenance history, and
streamlining the asset disposal process.



We have defined the acquire to dispose process here to also include financial
management or accounting processes of fixed assets and asset leases. This
includes the planning, budgeting, and management process for owned and leased
assets. By implementing Dynamics 365 to support the acquire to dispose process,
organizations can improve asset visibility, increase operational efficiency, and
reduce costs associated with asset management.

Description:
Classifying assets means organizing and categorizing assets based on specific
criteria such as type, usage, value, location, or lifecycle stage. This helps
organizations manage, track, and report on their assets more effectively. 

Common asset classifications include:
 * Tangible vs. Intangible (e.g., machinery vs. patents)
 * Current vs. Non-current (e.g., inventory vs. buildings)
 * IT assets, Facilities, Vehicles, etc.
 * Depreciation categories for accounting purposes

How Dynamics 365 Supports Asset Classification
Microsoft Dynamics 365, particularly in modules like Dynamics 365 Finance and
Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, provides robust tools for asset
classification:


Asset Types and Categories:

You can define asset types (e.g., equipment, vehicles) and assign them to
categories. Categories can include depreciation profiles, useful life, and
accounting rules.
 * Fixed Asset Management: Allows classification by asset group, location,
   department, and responsible employee. Supports tagging assets with custom
   attributes for more granular classification.
 * Hierarchical Structures: Assets can be grouped into parent-child
   relationships (e.g., a vehicle fleet with individual cars).
 * Lifecycle Tracking: Tracks assets from acquisition to disposal, with
   classification updates at each stage.
 * Reporting and Analytics: Enables filtering and reporting based on asset
   classifications for audits, budgeting, and compliance.

Title 6: Create and maintain asset type default in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Create, review, update, or remove asset type default setup using the captured Asset type defaults page. Asset type defaults define reusable maintenance defaults for combinations of asset type, manufacturer, and model. They help newly created or maintained assets inherit the appropriate warranty context, spare parts, and maintenance plans instead of requiring those relationships to be assembled separately for every asset.

Create only the combinations needed by the equipment population, using the General section to establish the asset type, manufacturer, model, and vendor warranty relationship. Maintain the Spare parts and Maintenance plans sections with approved defaults, and use the combination-creation function carefully when generating multiple records. Prerequisites include asset types, manufacturers and models, warranty setup, released spare-part items, and maintenance plans.

The defaults are consumed when the matching equipment context is used, supporting consistent maintenance planning and parts selection. Validate with representative manufacturer and model combinations: confirm the intended warranty, spare parts, and plans are available for the matching asset and that unrelated defaults do not appear. Review combinations when equipment models, vendor warranties, recommended spare parts, or preventive-maintenance strategies change, and retire obsolete defaults without removing historical context needed for existing assets.

Title 6: Create and maintain asset type in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Create, review, update, or remove asset type setup using the captured Asset types page. Asset types provide the primary classification for maintainable assets and determine which maintenance structures can be used with them. Every asset requires an asset type, making this configuration the organizing layer for lifecycle behavior, maintenance job types, counters, attributes, condition assessments, manufacturers, and models.

Define stable asset-type names that reflect meaningful equipment categories, then associate the approved asset lifecycle model. Configure the Maintenance job types, Counters, Attribute types, Condition assessments, and Manufacturers and models sections for each category. Coordinate these relationships with asset type defaults, warranties, spare parts, and maintenance plans. Avoid types that are either so broad that controls lose meaning or so narrow that each asset becomes its own category.

Asset types are consumed during asset creation and constrain the maintenance data and activities available for that asset. The deliverable graph confirms them as prerequisites for asset setup, preventive maintenance, mobile maintenance, and related operational scenarios. Validate by creating representative assets for each type and confirming lifecycle states, job types, counters, attributes, condition templates, manufacturers, and models are available as designed. Review types when the equipment portfolio or maintenance strategy changes.

Title 6: Create and maintain responsible maintenance worker in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Create, review, update, or remove responsible maintenance worker setup using the captured Responsible maintenance workers page. Responsible maintenance worker rules identify the worker or worker group expected to oversee maintenance requests or work orders for defined maintenance contexts. Responsibility can be related to asset types, individual assets, functional locations, maintenance job categories, job types, variants, or trades, and is distinct from the workers actually scheduled to perform the work.

Keep responsibility rules aligned with operational ownership and escalation practices, while using preferred-worker rules separately for scheduling preferences.

The responsible worker can be used on maintenance requests and work orders and may change as a request or work order moves through its lifecycle. Validate representative asset, location, trade, and job-type combinations, confirming that the intended responsible person or group is identified and that lifecycle updates behave as designed. Review the rules when organizational ownership, worker groups, asset structures, functional locations, maintenance processes, or lifecycle automation changes. Incomplete or conflicting rules can leave oversight unclear even when execution resources are successfully scheduled.

Title 6: Create and maintain asset criticality in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Create, review, update, or remove asset criticality setup using the captured Asset criticalities page. Asset criticalities assign a criticality value to assets or asset contexts so maintenance work reflects the operational consequence of an asset being unavailable. The assigned criticality is transferred to work orders and contributes to work order criticality during scheduling; it is not intended to be changed independently on the work order.

Before assigning criticalities, define the organization's criticality types and scoring factors. Establish which functional locations, asset types, manufacturers, models, or individual assets require differentiated assignments and agree on governance with maintenance and operations owners. Use the most specific assignment needed to represent business impact without creating contradictory or redundant rules.

The resulting value is consumed when work orders are created and prioritized for scheduling, helping distinguish maintenance that has greater production or productivity impact. Validate by assigning different criticality contexts to representative assets, creating work orders, and confirming the inherited criticality and scheduling score behave as intended. Review assignments when assets move, production dependencies change, equipment is replaced, or risk assessments are updated because stale criticality can distort maintenance priorities.

Title 6: Create and maintain maintenance downtime reason code in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Create, review, update, or remove maintenance downtime reason code setup using the captured Maintenance downtime reason codes page. Maintenance downtime reason codes classify why an asset or production machine was unavailable during maintenance. They provide a consistent vocabulary for distinguishing planned stops, breakdowns, and other causes when downtime is registered against the asset selected on a work order.

Before configuration, agree the reason categories needed for maintenance and production analysis, their naming convention, and the ownership process for adding or retiring values. Keep reasons mutually understandable and avoid duplicate codes that describe the same operational cause. Coordinate the list with work order practices and with the teams responsible for production availability and maintenance performance reporting.

The codes are selected when maintenance downtime registrations are created and therefore affect how asset stoppages can be reviewed and compared. Validate each code by recording representative planned and unplanned downtime for an asset on a work order and confirming that users can select the intended reason and interpret it consistently in downtime records. Review the list when maintenance strategies, production-loss classifications, equipment populations, or reporting requirements change; uncontrolled changes can fragment historical analysis and obscure recurring causes of lost availability.

depending on multiple parameters. In case the asset is acquired, it goes through
a high-level process that could be a mix of more asset related information
adjustment, depreciation, disposal. Companies can define rules to record
acquisition method, depreciation and disposal, write-ups and write-downs.



The management of assets and its finance is an ongoing operational process for
an organization. It becomes more important when audits are executed to review
financial information.

Title 5: Extend an asset lease in Dynamics 365 Finance
Description:
For organizations that adhere to ASC 842 or IFRS 16, a lease is remeasured to
reflect a change in the present value of the future minimum lease payments
(PVFMLP). If the PVFMLP increases, the journal entry that is created will be a
debit to the right-of-use (ROU) asset account and a credit to the lease
liability account for the difference between the new PVFMLP and the previous
PVFMLP. If the PVFMLP decreases, the journal entry will be a debit to the lease
liability account and a credit to the ROU asset account for the difference. If
the adjustment decreases the ROU asset past 0 (zero), the remainder is credited
to the gain on lease modification posting account that is specified on the Lease
posting accounts page. The system accounts for these transactions and other
adjustment entries, such as classification changes, initial direct costs, lease
incentives, prepayments, and dismantling costs that arise from lease
modifications.

Title 5: Refurbish rental fleet assets in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description: Plan and record major refurbishment that improves the condition, capability, or useful life of rental fleet assets.

In many organizations, the terms maintenance and repair are used
interchangeably. However, they might refer to different areas in the asset
management process. Maintenance includes activities that can be scheduled and/or
performed at a specific time to help prevent assets from breaking down and
increase their life. Repairs help restore the functionality of assets when they
are damaged or inoperable from a process standpoint.




There are three main types of maintenance tasks:

 * Reactive: Reactive maintenance involves repairing an asset that has broken
   down or experienced a failure, typically one that isn't critical for
   business. If the maintenance strategy isn't effectively planned for the

Create, review, update, or remove scheduled execution setup using the captured Scheduled execution page. They give planners flexibility to express that a job should be completed within a day, week, or other operating window, enabling available workers to take nearby eligible work while still respecting maintenance commitments.

Configure service levels first, then determine how broadly each scheduled-execution line should apply. Rules can be general or narrowed by maintenance context such as work order type, asset type, or maintenance job type. Review the setup when service commitments, maintenance strategies, workforce capacity, asset criticality, or planning horizons change. Incorrect or overlapping rules can make urgent work appear flexible or constrain routine work unnecessarily, reducing scheduling efficiency.

In the rapidly evolving business environment of today, for any organization, the
process of retiring and disposing of assets holds a pivotal role in the
lifecycle management of resources within that organization. The retire and
dispose of assets business process involves retiring and disposing of fixed
assets that are no longer needed. It also covers when assets must be replaced by
assessing the lifecycle stage, usability, and alignment of assets with the
organizational goals.




As assets mature, outgrow their usefulness, or no longer fit the evolving
demands of the business, or as technology evolves, the strategic choice to
retire and dispose of assets is crucial. Making informed decisions about their
retirement and disposal ensures that the organization maintains operational
efficiency, optimizes resource allocation, and adheres to legal and
environmental responsibilities.



When a fixed asset is no longer needed, it can either be scrapped or sold. If
the asset still has value, it's likely to be set to be sold. When a fixed asset
is sold with profit, the profit is recognized in the year of the sale, and then
it's posted to the profit and loss part of the chart of accounts.

differences between information loaded into the Lease import framework and the
information that's currently in the system. This lets you compare what was
adjusted, updated, or added through the Lease import framework. The values in
the report will vary based on the selected lease. The report will only show
those fields that differ from what is currently in the system and what is in the
staging tables. The old value is what is either currently in the system or what
was previously in the system, depending on whether the import process has run.
The new value shows the value that's in the staging table that will replace the
old value. The Lease modification report shows all leases that have been
modified within a specified date range. The report also shows the user who
adjusted the lease, and the total amount of liability adjusted. The Lease
movement report serves as a roll forward report for the lease liability balances
for each lease. This report allows the user to view the liability transactions
of a lease during a specified period. The Lease transactions inquiry shows all
the journal entries that have been generated by Asset leasing. Each journal
entry is linked with the book ID it was originated from. This lets you easily
associate the journal entry with corresponding lease. The Lease transactions
inquiry functions in a manner that's similar to the Voucher transactions page in

and issues. The process involves various steps, such as engaging with customers,
logging the case, assigning it to the appropriate team or individual,
investigating and resolving the issue, and closing the case. However, managing
this process can be challenging, particularly as organizations grow in size and
complexity, which is where technology solutions like Dynamics 365 come in.




Microsoft Business Applications including Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams, and
Microsoft 365 are a powerful platform that can support the case to resolution
process by automating and streamlining many of its key steps. For example,
Dynamics 365 Customer Service can enable organizations to engage in
conversations with customers through various channels, including email, phone,
chat and social media, identify and authenticate customers, answer customer
questions, run transactions on behalf of customers, log cases and automatically
assign cases to the appropriate team or individual based on predefined rules. It
can also provide real-time visibility into case status and progress, enabling
managers and teams to track performance, identify bottlenecks, and optimize the
process for greater efficiency and effectiveness. Dynamics 365 Human Resources
has functionality to help employees and managers communicate effectively through
cases to manage common requests and issues. Likewise, Dynamics 365 Supply Chain
Management includes cases management tools to help with the process of managing

product recall. Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management also include
tools to help with the effective management of returns, exchanges, credits,
price matching, and more.



However, it's important to note that Dynamics 365 is just one component of a
broader case to resolution process. The process involves multiple stakeholders,
such as customers, employees, managers, and support teams, who may have
different roles, responsibilities, and workflows. Moreover, the process may
differ depending on the type of case, the industry, or the organization's
specific requirements. Therefore, it's important to have a well-defined and
flexible process that can adapt to different scenarios and needs, and to ensure
that Dynamics 365 is integrated with other systems and processes for maximum
effectiveness.



Every organization has variations to the case to resolution process. Here, we
define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology

Security Roles for Creating Knowledge Base Articles in D365 Customer Service

In Dynamics 365 Customer Service, users need specific security roles to create
and manage knowledge base (KB) articles. The key roles involved in KB management
include:

 1. Knowledge Manager – Full control over knowledge articles, including
    publishing and managing content.
 2. Knowledge Author – Can create, edit, and submit knowledge articles but does
    not have publishing permissions.
 3. Customer Service Manager – Can manage customer service operations, including
    knowledge articles.
 4. Customer Service Representative – Typically has read-only access to
    published knowledge articles but may have permissions to create drafts.
 5. System Administrator – Has full access, including the ability to configure
    knowledge management settings.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEPS TO CREATE A KNOWLEDGE BASE ARTICLE IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Follow these steps to create a KB article in Dynamics 365 Customer Service:

STEP 1: NAVIGATE TO KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT

 1. Sign in to Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
 2. In the Customer Service Workspace, select Knowledge Articles from the left
    navigation pane.

STEP 2: CREATE A NEW KNOWLEDGE ARTICLE

 1. Click + New to create a new article.
 2. Fill in the required fields:
    * Title – Enter a meaningful title.
    * Content – Add the main content of the article in the rich text editor.
    * Keywords – Add keywords to improve searchability.
    * Description – Provide a summary of the article.
    * Expiration Date – Set if applicable.
    * Subject – Categorize the article under relevant subjects.

STEP 3: ADD ATTACHMENTS (OPTIONAL)

 * If needed, attach images, documents, or other reference materials.

STEP 4: REVIEW AND SUBMIT FOR APPROVAL

 1. Click Save to draft the article.
 2. Click Submit to send the article for review.
 3. If approval is required, a Knowledge Manager will review and approve/reject
    it.

STEP 5: PUBLISH THE ARTICLE

 1. Once approved, click Publish to make the article available to users.
 2. Choose the publishing options:
    * Internal – Visible only to employees.
    * External – Available to customers via the self-service portal.
    * Restricted – Limited access based on permissions.

Description:
As a Knowledge Manager, I need to know how to review existing articles, identify
updates, and provide the updates in knowledge base articles so that they can be
reviewed/approved so the updated content is available to support analysts.  





1. Reviewing Knowledge Base Articles

A structured review process ensures that KB articles remain useful and
up-to-date. This includes:


A. IDENTIFYING ARTICLES FOR REVIEW

 * Use expiration dates and review schedules to trigger a review.
 * Monitor article feedback (user ratings, comments, and usage stats).
 * Use search analytics to determine if articles are effectively addressing
   customer needs.
 * Assign review responsibility to a Knowledge Manager or a designated team.


B. EVALUATING ARTICLES

 * Relevance: Is the article still applicable to current products, services, or
   processes?
 * Accuracy: Does the content contain outdated information or incorrect details?
 * Clarity: Is the article well-structured, concise, and easy to understand?
 * Format & Compliance: Does it adhere to KB style guidelines and regulatory
   requirements?

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. UPDATING KNOWLEDGE BASE ARTICLES

Once an article is identified for update, follow these steps:


A. INITIATE THE UPDATE PROCESS

 * The assigned editor or SME (Subject Matter Expert) creates a new draft
   version of the article.
 * Changes should align with corporate guidelines, product updates, or new best
   practices.


B. EDITING AND REVISING

 * Make necessary content updates (text, images, embedded videos, or links).
 * Ensure formatting meets KB standards (structured sections like Overview,
   Steps, FAQs).
 * Tag the article with relevant categories and keywords for better
   discoverability.


C. INTERNAL REVIEW BY PEERS

 * A peer or Knowledge Author verifies the technical accuracy of the changes.
 * The article is checked for grammar, clarity, and formatting consistency.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


3. SUBMITTING FOR APPROVAL

Before publishing, the article must go through an approval process:


A. REVIEWER ASSIGNMENT

 * A designated reviewer or approver (Knowledge Manager, QA, or Team Lead) is
   assigned.
 * The reviewer gets notified via D365 workflows or Power Automate.


B. REVIEW PROCESS

 * The reviewer validates content accuracy, completeness, and policy compliance.
 * They provide comments or request changes if needed.
 * If changes are needed, the article is sent back for revision.


C. APPROVAL AND PUBLISHING

 * Once approved, the article moves to a published state.
 * It becomes available in the Customer Service portal, internal support
   interface, or chatbot integration.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


4. ONGOING MAINTENANCE AND GOVERNANCE

 * Regular Reviews: Schedule a periodic review cycle (e.g., every 6 months).
 * Feedback Incorporation: Address customer feedback and internal team
   suggestions.
 * Archival of Old Articles: Remove or retire articles that are no longer
   relevant.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


WORKFLOW IN DYNAMICS 365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

 1. Identify articles needing updates (scheduled review, feedback, analytics).
 2. Edit & Draft the article with necessary updates.
 3. Submit for Review to an assigned reviewer.
 4. Approve & Publish once the reviewer confirms accuracy.
 5. Monitor & Maintain articles using review schedules and feedback.

Description:
As a user / HR Manager, I need to understand the process of defining an agent
skill set, including required skills, gaps, training plans, so that support
analysts/agents are assigned to the proper skills to support the areas they are
best suited.



Defining Agent Skill Set in D365 Case Management is part of Omnichannel for
Customer Service and Unified Routing. It plays a crucial role in intelligent
case routing but is not a mandatory prerequisite for basic case creation.
However, if you're implementing automated case routing and queue management,
agent skill definitions should be configured.


WHERE TO DEFINE AGENT SKILL SETS?

Agent skills are primarily set up in the Customer Service Admin
Center or Omnichannel for Customer Service under the Work Distribution and
Routing settings.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEPS TO DEFINE AGENT SKILL SET FOR CASE ROUTING

 1. Enable Unified Routing (If Not Already Enabled)
    
    * Go to Customer Service Admin Center > Work Distribution > Unified Routing.
    * Enable Unified Routing to allow intelligent case assignments.

 2. Define Skills
    
    * Navigate to Customer Service Admin Center > Agent Experiences > Skills.
    * Click New Skill and define:
      * Skill Name (e.g., "Warranty Claims Processing").
      * Skill Category (Optional for grouping).
      * Skill Proficiency Levels (Optional: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced).

 3. Assign Skills to Agents
    
    * Go to Customer Service Admin Center > Agent Experiences > Agent Profiles.
    * Select an Agent Profile or create a new one.
    * Assign skills based on expertise.

 4. Configure Skill-Based Routing Rules
    
    * Navigate to Work Distribution & Routing > Routing Rulesets.
    * Define a new Routing Rule for cases based on attributes like:
      * Case Type
      * Case Subject
      * Customer Priority
      * Entitlement
    * Assign the rule to a queue with agents who have the required skills.

 5. Assign Agents to Queues
    
    * Go to Workstreams > Create a Workstream (or modify an existing one).
    * Add Skill Matching Criteria to route cases based on agent skills.
    * Assign Agents to queues based on their defined skills.

 6. Enable Auto-Assignment of Cases to Agents
    
    * Ensure auto-assignment is enabled within Routing & Work Distribution.
    * Cases will now be assigned to the best-matched agent based on skill
      proficiency.


HOW IT WORKS IN CASE MANAGEMENT?

 * When a case is created, unified routing checks agent availability, assigned
   skills, and proficiency.
 * The system intelligently routes the case to the best-qualified agent.
 * If no skilled agent is available, fallback rules (such as routing to a
   general queue) apply.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


WHERE DOES THIS FIT IN THE CASE CREATION PROCESS?

Agent skill set definition fits under Step 4 (Queues & Routing) in case
management setup. While not mandatory for case creation, it is essential for
intelligent case assignment.

Description:
Title: As a Customer Service Manager, I want to understand how to define Teams
and Queues within D365 Customer Service so that cases are routed efficiently to
the correct team and queue.





DEFINING QUEUES AND TEAMS IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Queues and Teams are essential components in D365 Customer Service for managing
and routing cases efficiently. Queues help organize and distribute work items,
while Teams group users together based on roles, expertise, or business
functions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. DEFINING QUEUES IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

A Queue is a collection of work items (Cases, Activities, Emails, etc.) that can
be assigned to users or teams for resolution.


STEPS TO CREATE A QUEUE

 1. Go to the Power Platform Admin Center → Select your D365 Customer Service
    App.
 2. Navigate to Customer Service Hub → Service Management → Queues.
 3. Click New to create a new queue.
 4. Fill in the details:
    * Name: E.g., "Warranty Claims Queue"
    * Type:
      * Public: Any user can work on queue items.
      * Private: Only assigned users can access the queue.
    * Incoming Email (if using email-to-case routing).
    * Associated Team (Optional): Links the queue to a team for better work
      distribution.
 5. Save and Close.


TYPES OF QUEUES

 * Default Queue: Assigned automatically to each user and team.
 * Custom Queues: Specific to business processes (e.g., "High Priority Cases").
 * Routing Queues: Used in Omnichannel for automated case routing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. DEFINING TEAMS IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

A Team is a group of users who share ownership of records and work
collaboratively.


STEPS TO CREATE A TEAM

 1. Go to Power Platform Admin Center → Advanced Settings.
 2. Navigate to Settings → Security → Teams.
 3. Click New and enter:
    * Team Name: E.g., "Warranty Support Team"
    * Business Unit: Assign to the correct unit.
    * Team Type:
      * Owner Team (Default) – Can own records.
      * Access Team – Can only collaborate but not own records.
    * Queue Association: (Optional) Assign a default queue for the team.
 4. Add Users to the Team.
 5. Save and Close.

(BPF) for case management so that agents follow a structured, step-by-step
approach to resolving customer issues efficiently and consistently





STEPS TO DEFINE A BUSINESS PROCESS FLOW (BPF) IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

A Business Process Flow (BPF) in Dynamics 365 Customer Service guides users
through a structured sequence of stages to ensure consistent case resolution.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. ACCESS THE BUSINESS PROCESS FLOW DESIGNER

 1. Navigate to Power Apps (https://make.powerapps.com).
 2. Select the Environment where you want to create the BPF.
 3. Go to Solutions (or create a new solution to store the BPF).
 4. Click New → Select Process.
 5. In the Create Process dialog:
    * Process Name: e.g., "Case Resolution Process"
    * Category: Business Process Flow
    * Entity: Case
    * Click Create.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. DEFINE STAGES & STEPS IN THE BUSINESS PROCESS FLOW

A BPF consists of Stages (phases) and Steps (fields to be filled in each stage).


EXAMPLE STAGES FOR CASE MANAGEMENT:

 1. Identify Issue
    
    * Step 1: Enter Case Title (Required).
    * Step 2: Select Case Type (Problem, Request, Inquiry).

 2. Investigate
    
    * Step 1: Assign to an Agent or Queue.
    * Step 2: Capture Customer Notes or Attachments.
    * Step 3: Set Case Priority.

 3. Resolve
    
    * Step 1: Enter Resolution Details.
    * Step 2: Confirm Customer Satisfaction.

 4. Close Case
    
    * Step 1: Mark Case as Resolved or Escalated.
    * Step 2: Generate Closure Summary Report.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


3. CONFIGURE CONDITIONAL BRANCHING (IF NEEDED)

 * If Case Type = "High Priority", route it to a Supervisor Review stage.
 * If Case Resolution Time > 24 hours, escalate the case automatically.

To configure branching:

 1. Click the Stage where you want a decision point.
 2. Click Add Condition.
 3. Define logic (e.g., "If Case Priority = High, move to Escalation Stage").
 4. Apply conditions and save.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


4. SET REQUIRED FIELDS & PERMISSIONS

 * Mark important fields as Required to ensure data entry before moving to the
   next stage.
 * Assign security roles to control who can modify the BPF.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


5. ACTIVATE AND PUBLISH THE BPF

 1. Click Validate to check for errors.
 2. Click Save and then Activate.
 3. Publish the BPF so users can see it in Case Records.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


BONUS: TRACKING & REPORTING ON BPF PROGRESS

 * Use Dashboards to track how long cases stay in each stage.
 * Create Power BI reports to analyze case resolution efficiency.

Operating hours in Dynamics 365 Customer Service define the availability

case escalations, response times, and agent availability are aligned with
business hours.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. STEPS TO DEFINE OPERATING HOURS IN D365


STEP 1: NAVIGATE TO THE CUSTOMER SERVICE ADMIN CENTER

   available.


STEP 5: VALIDATE AND PUBLISH

    behavior.

Description:
As a Customer Support Manager, I want to assign cases to the appropriate team,
individual, or queue so that cases are handled by the right people and resolved
efficiently.


PROCESS FOR ASSIGNING A CASE TO A TEAM, INDIVIDUAL, OR QUEUE IN D365 CUSTOMER
SERVICE

Assigning cases correctly in D365 Customer Service ensures that the right team,
individual, or queue handles the case efficiently, improving response times and
resolution rates.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. STEPS TO ASSIGN A CASE TO A TEAM, INDIVIDUAL, OR QUEUE


STEP 1: OPEN THE CASE RECORD

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Workspace.
 2. In the left navigation, go to Cases.
 3. Open the case that needs to be assigned.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 2: CHOOSE ASSIGNMENT METHOD

A. ASSIGN TO AN INDIVIDUAL

 1. Click on the Assign button in the top action bar.
 2. In the Assign To window, select User.
 3. Search for and select the User to assign the case to.
 4. Click Assign.
    The case is now owned by the selected individual.

B. ASSIGN TO A TEAM

 1. Click Assign.
 2. In the Assign To window, select Team.
 3. Search for and select the Team.
 4. Click Assign.
    The case is now owned by the selected team, and any team member can work on
    it.

C. ASSIGN TO A QUEUE (FOR AUTOMATIC OR SHARED WORK HANDLING)

 1. Open the Case Record.
 2. Locate the Queue field.
 3. Click Change Queue and select the appropriate queue.
 4. Click Save & Close.
    ✅ The case is now assigned to a queue, and available agents can pick it up.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 3: AUTOMATE ASSIGNMENT USING ROUTING RULES (OPTIONAL)

If cases should be assigned automatically, configure Routing Rules:

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Admin Center.
 2. Go to Work Distribution & Routing → Routing Rule Sets.
 3. Define rules based on case priority, type, or customer.
 4. Assign cases directly to a queue, team, or user.
    Cases are now automatically routed based on predefined rules.

Title 4: Create a case from a channel
Description:
As a Customer Support Manager, I want to ensure that cases are automatically
created from various customer channels so that issues are tracked efficiently
and resolved promptly.






STEPS TO CREATE A CASE FROM DIFFERENT CHANNELS IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Cases can be created manually by agents or automatically when customer
interactions come from various channels like chat, phone calls, portal requests,
emails, and product returns.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEPS TO CREATE A CASE FROM DIFFERENT CHANNELS





A. CREATE A CASE FROM A CHAT (OMNICHANNEL FOR CUSTOMER SERVICE)

 1. Enable Omnichannel for Customer Service in Customer Service Admin Center.
 2. Customer starts a chat session via Live Chat, SMS, or WhatsApp.
 3. Agent receives the chat in the Omnichannel Agent Dashboard.
 4. Click Create Case directly from the chat window.
 5. The system auto-fills:
    * Customer Name (if authenticated).
    * Case Origin = Chat.
    * Conversation Details from the chat.
 6. Agent enters additional details and clicks Save & Close.
    The case is now linked to the chat conversation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


B. CREATE A CASE FROM A LIVE PHONE CALL IN OMNICHANNEL

 1. Open Omnichannel for Customer Service.
 2. Navigate to the Omnichannel Agent Dashboard.
 3. When a phone call request arrives, click Accept.
 4. The call session will open in the conversation panel.
 5. Click More Actions (⋮) → Create Case.
 6. A new Case Form will open with the following auto-filled details:
    * Customer Name
    * Case Origin = Phone Call
    * Call Transcript or Notes (if enabled)
 7. Enter additional details:
    * Case Title (brief issue summary).
    * Case Type (Inquiry, Complaint, Service Request, etc.).
    * Priority (Low, Normal, High, Critical).
    * Detailed Description of the issue.
 8. Assign the case to a specific agent, team, or queue (or let Routing
    Rules assign it automatically).
 9. Click Save & Close to link the case to the phone call session.
    The phone call is logged, and the case is linked for further resolution.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


C. CREATE A CASE FROM A PORTAL REQUEST

 1. Customer submits a request via the Customer Self-Service Portal.
 2. The system automatically creates a case when the request is submitted.
 3. The Case Record is auto-populated with:
    * Customer Name & Contact Info.
    * Case Title & Description (from the form submission).
    * Case Origin = Portal.
 4. Case routing rules assign the case to a team or queue.
 5. Customer receives an automated email confirmation.
    The case is now in the system and ready for an agent to process.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


D. CREATE A CASE FROM AN EMAIL

 1. Enable Email-to-Case Automation in Customer Service Admin Center.
 2. Customer sends an email to a designated support email address.
 3. The system automatically:
    * Creates a Case Record.
    * Links the email conversation to the case.
    * Sets Case Origin = Email.
 4. The case is placed in the Email Queue, ready for assignment.
    Agents can now respond directly from the case record.

STEPS TO MANUALLY CREATE A CASE IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Creating a case manually ensures that customer issues are properly tracked and
assigned, especially for cases such as customer complaints, product returns, and
disputed invoices.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. STEPS TO MANUALLY CREATE A CASE


STEP 1: OPEN CUSTOMER SERVICE WORKSPACE

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Workspace in Dynamics 365.
 2. Click on Cases from the left navigation panel.
 3. Click New Case to open the case creation form.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 2: ENTER GENERAL CASE INFORMATION

 1. Customer Information
    
    * Select Customer Name (Contact or Account).
    * Add Primary Contact (if applicable).

 2. Case Classification
    
    * Case Title → Briefly describe the issue (e.g., "Damaged Product
      Received").
    * Case Type → Select from predefined categories (e.g., Complaint, Product
      Return, Billing Issue).
    * Case Subject → Select a relevant subject (e.g., "Shipping Issues",
      "Billing Disputes").
    * Priority → Set based on urgency (Low, Normal, High, Critical).

 3. Case Origin
    
    * Choose how the issue was reported (Phone, Email, Chat, Web, In-Person).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 3: CAPTURE SPECIFIC CASE DETAILS BASED ON TYPE

A. EXAMPLE BASED ON CUSTOMER COMPLAINT

 1. Case Type: Complaint
 2. Description: Document the customer’s concern in detail.
 3. Attachments: Upload any supporting files (screenshots, email evidence).
 4. Resolution Expectations: Document what the customer expects as a resolution.
 5. Assign Case:
    * Assign to Customer Relations Team or a specific agent.
    * Use Routing Rules if automated assignment is enabled.
 6. Click Save & Close or Save & Continue.
    The customer complaint case is logged and ready for resolution.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

B. EXAMPLE BASED ON PRODUCT RETURN CASE

 1. Case Type: Product Return
 2. Order Number: Link the case to the corresponding order.
 3. Reason for Return: Select from predefined options (Defective, Wrong Item,
    Not Needed).
 4. Return Process:
    * Attach return documents (receipts, images of the product).
    * Provide shipping instructions if necessary.
 5. Assign Case:
    * Assign to Returns Processing Team.
    * Move the case to a Product Return Queue.
 6. Click Save & Close.
    The product return case is created and linked to the order.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

C. EXAMPLE BASED ON DISPUTED INVOICE CASE

 1. Case Type: Billing Issue
 2. Invoice Number: Enter or search for the disputed invoice.
 3. Dispute Reason: Select from predefined options (Incorrect Amount, Duplicate
    Charge, Unauthorized Charge).
 4. Supporting Evidence: Attach relevant documents (invoice copy, payment
    receipt, customer email).
 5. Resolution Process:
    * Specify the next steps (review invoice, credit/refund processing).
    * Assign case to Billing/Accounts Team.
 6. Click Save & Close.
    The disputed invoice case is logged and ready for financial review.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 4: FOLLOW UP & TRACK CASE PROGRESS

 1. Use Case Timeline to document updates and customer follow-ups.
 2. Attach relevant Knowledge Base Articles for agent reference.
 3. Set up SLA tracking to ensure timely resolution.
 4. If needed, escalate the case to a higher-priority team.

Description:
AS A CUSTOMER SERVICE REPRESENTATIVE (CSR),
I WANT TO AUTOMATICALLY NOTIFY CUSTOMERS WHEN A NEW CASE IS CREATED, UPDATED, OR
RESOLVED,
SO THAT I CAN ENSURE TIMELY COMMUNICATION, REDUCE MANUAL EFFORT, AND IMPROVE
CUSTOMER SATISFACTION.



PROCESS FOR SENDING CUSTOMER NOTIFICATIONS IN D365 CE FOR CASE MANAGEMENT

This document outlines the process and detailed steps for automatically sending
notifications to customers in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement (D365
CE) when a new case is created, updated, or resolved.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. PROCESS OVERVIEW


NOTIFICATION SCENARIOS

 * New Case Acknowledgment: When a new case is created, the customer should
   receive a confirmation email with case details.
 * Case Update Notification: When a case is updated (status change, assigned
   agent change, or important notes added), the customer should be informed.
 * Case Resolution Notification: When a case is resolved or closed, the customer
   should receive a resolution summary.


TECHNOLOGY USED

 * Power Automate: Automates email notifications triggered by case events.
 * D365 Email Templates: Predefined templates ensure consistent messaging.
 * Dataverse Triggers: Listens for case events in the system.
 * SMS Gateway (Optional): For SMS notifications if required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. PROCESS WORKFLOW


STEP 1: TRIGGER SETUP (DEFINE EVENT)

Define the trigger event for each type of notification:

 * New Case Acknowledgment → Triggered when a new case is created.
 * Case Update Notification → Triggered when a case status, owner, or priority
   is updated.
 * Case Resolution Notification → Triggered when a case is marked as "Resolved"
   or "Closed."


STEP 2: FETCH CUSTOMER DETAILS

 * Retrieve the customer's email or preferred notification channel from the Case
   record.
 * Get related Account or Contact information.


STEP 3: SELECT NOTIFICATION TEMPLATE

 * Use Email Templates in D365 CE for consistent messaging.
 * Personalize the template with:
   * Case Number
   * Case Title
   * Current Status
   * Assigned Agent
   * Resolution Summary (for closed cases)
   * Case Portal Link (if applicable)


STEP 4: SEND NOTIFICATION VIA POWER AUTOMATE

 1. New Case Acknowledgment:
    
    * Trigger: When a new case is created.
    * Action: Send an email to the customer with the case number and SLA
      details.

 2. Case Update Notification:
    
    * Trigger: When an important field changes (status, priority, owner, or a
      significant note is added).
    * Action: Send an update email or SMS with the latest case details.

 3. Case Resolution Notification:
    
    * Trigger: When a case status is changed to "Resolved" or "Closed."
    * Action: Send a resolution summary to the customer with next steps or
      feedback request.


STEP 5: LOG NOTIFICATION IN CASE TIMELINE

 * Create a Case Timeline entry in D365 CE for audit purposes.
 * Store notification details, including:
   * Timestamp
   * Email content
   * Customer response (if applicable)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


3. DETAILED STEPS IN POWER AUTOMATE

Below are the detailed steps for implementing this using Power Automate.


A. FLOW FOR NEW CASE ACKNOWLEDGMENT

 1. Trigger: When a new Case is created in D365 CE (Dataverse trigger).
 2. Action: Retrieve related Contact/Account details.
 3. Action: Retrieve the "New Case Acknowledgment" email template.
 4. Action: Personalize the email with case details.
 5. Action: Send an email to the customer.
 6. Action (Optional): Send an SMS if preferred.
 7. Action: Log the notification in the Case Timeline.


B. FLOW FOR CASE UPDATE NOTIFICATION

 1. Trigger: When a Case record is updated (Dataverse modified trigger).
 2. Condition: Check if key fields changed (Status, Priority, Assigned Agent,
    Notes).
 3. Action: Retrieve the "Case Update" email template.
 4. Action: Send the email to the customer.
 5. Action: Log the notification in the Case Timeline.


C. FLOW FOR CASE RESOLUTION NOTIFICATION

 1. Trigger: When a Case status changes to "Resolved" or "Closed."
 2. Action: Retrieve the "Case Resolution" email template.
 3. Action: Personalize the email with resolution details and next steps.
 4. Action: Send an email with a customer feedback link.
 5. Action: Log the notification in the Case Timeline.

Description:
As a Customer Service Representative (CSR),

I want to communicate with customers via chat, email, phone, or in-person, So
that I can provide timely support and ensure cases are handled efficiently.




his document outlines the standard process and steps for handling customer cases
in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service, including engaging with customers
via chat, email, phone, or in-person interactions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. PROCESS OVERVIEW

The case management process ensures efficient tracking, resolution, and
communication with customers across multiple channels. The key steps include:

 1. Case Creation – Capture customer issues from different channels.
 2. Case Triage & Assignment – Prioritize and assign the case to the right
    agent.
 3. Customer Engagement & Communication – Interact with the customer through
    their preferred channel (chat, email, phone, or in-person).
 4. Case Investigation & Resolution – Diagnose and work towards resolving the
    issue.
 5. Case Closure & Follow-up – Provide resolution confirmation and gather
    customer feedback.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. DETAILED STEPS IN THE CASE MANAGEMENT PROCESS


STEP 1: CASE CREATION

 * Cases can be created manually by a CSR, automatically from customer
   interactions, or via a self-service portal.
 * Supported case creation methods:
   * Email: An email received creates a case (via Email-to-Case automation).
   * Chat: Live chat sessions initiate a case.
   * Phone Call: A CSR logs a case from an inbound or outbound call.
   * In-Person: A CSR manually logs the issue after an in-person conversation.
   * Self-Service Portal: Customers submit cases via a support portal.

Action Items:


 * Ensure customer details (contact, account, and issue description) are
   correctly captured.
 * Assign a priority and category for the case.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 2: CASE TRIAGE & ASSIGNMENT

 * Automatic Assignment: Based on skill set, availability, or workload
   via Omnichannel for Customer Service or Workstreams.
 * Manual Assignment: A supervisor or dispatcher assigns the case.
 * Prioritization Rules: Cases are categorized as Low, Normal, High, or
   Urgent based on impact.

Action Items:


 * Ensure the correct agent is assigned.
 * Add internal notes if required for additional context.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 3: CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT & COMMUNICATION

The agent initiates or continues communication with the customer based on their
preferred channel:

1. LIVE CHAT (OMNICHANNEL FOR CUSTOMER SERVICE)

 * Customer starts a conversation via chat.
 * The CSR greets the customer and reviews previous interactions (if available).
 * CSR works on resolving the issue in real-time.
 * If further action is needed, the chat is converted into a case for follow-up.

2. EMAIL (CUSTOMER TIMELINE IN D365)

 * CSR responds to customer emails directly within the Case record.
 * Email templates can be used for standard responses.
 * Attachments (screenshots, guides, etc.) can be included.
 * If necessary, an escalation email is sent to internal teams.

3. PHONE CALL (INTEGRATED SOFTPHONE OR MANUAL ENTRY)

 * CSR calls the customer and logs the conversation in the Case Timeline.
 * Key details such as call duration, discussion points, and next steps are
   recorded.
 * If needed, the call is transferred to a different team or escalated.

4. IN-PERSON MEETING (FIELD VISIT OR WALK-IN)

 * If the customer visits the support center or an agent is dispatched onsite,
   notes are logged.
 * Customer signs off on discussions or agreements, if applicable.
 * Any necessary follow-up actions are scheduled.

Action Items:


 * Keep conversation history logged in the Case Timeline for visibility.
 * Ensure follow-up tasks (if needed) are scheduled.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 4: CASE INVESTIGATION & RESOLUTION

 * The CSR diagnoses the issue using knowledge articles, past cases, or internal
   resources.
 * If needed, the case is escalated to technical support or a manager.
 * If a product return, refund, or service visit is required, the proper process
   is initiated.
 * A resolution is determined and communicated to the customer.

Action Items:


 * Use Knowledge Base articles to assist in troubleshooting.
 * Escalate the case if additional expertise is required.
 * Document resolution steps in the case record.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 5: CASE CLOSURE & FOLLOW-UP

 * The agent confirms with the customer that the issue is resolved.
 * The case is marked as “Resolved” in D365 Customer Service.
 * A feedback survey is sent to the customer (optional).
 * If unresolved, the case is reopened for further action.

Action Items:


 * Update the case with final resolution notes.
 * Notify the customer and confirm resolution before closing the case.
 * (Optional) Send a post-resolution survey for customer feedback.

Description:
As a Customer Service Representative (CSR),
I want to create and track tasks related to a case,
So that I can ensure all necessary actions are completed for resolution.





STEPS TO CREATE AND TRACK TASKS FOR A CASE IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

In Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service, tasks help agents track actions
related to resolving customer cases. This document outlines the steps to create,
assign, and track tasks associated with a case.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. PROCESS OVERVIEW

When working on a case, tasks can be created to:

 * Assign follow-up actions to an agent or team.
 * Track pending actions such as investigations, customer callbacks, or
   approvals.
 * Ensure that all case-related activities are completed before closing the
   case.

Tasks can be managed through the Activities pane in the Case record.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. STEPS TO CREATE A TASK FOR A CASE


STEP 1: NAVIGATE TO THE CASE RECORD

 1. Open Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
 2. Go to Service > Cases.
 3. Select an existing case or create a new one.


STEP 2: ADD A NEW TASK

As a Customer Service Representative (CSR),
I want to follow up on a case internally, with a customer, or with a vendor,
So that I can ensure timely updates, track progress, and resolve the issue
efficiently.





STEPS TO FOLLOW UP ON A CASE IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Effective case follow-ups ensure timely resolution and maintain strong
communication between internal teams, customers, and vendors. This guide
outlines the steps for:

 1. Internal Case Follow-up (within the organization)
 2. Customer Case Follow-up (keeping customers informed)
 3. Vendor Case Follow-up (escalating cases to third-party vendors)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. INTERNAL CASE FOLLOW-UP (WITHIN THE ORGANIZATION)


STEP 1: IDENTIFY FOLLOW-UP NEEDS

 * Open the Case Record in D365 Customer Service.
 * Check the Status, Assigned Agent, and Notes to determine if internal
   follow-up is required.


STEP 2: ASSIGN OR ESCALATE THE CASE

 * If additional expertise is needed, assign the case to another team or
   escalate.
 * Use the Case Owner field to change ownership.
 * Add an Internal Note with instructions or context.


STEP 3: SCHEDULE A TASK FOR INTERNAL FOLLOW-UP

 * Click + Add Activity > Task within the Case Timeline.
 * Assign the task to an internal team member with a due date.
 * Mark the task as In Progress or Waiting for Input.


STEP 4: FOLLOW-UP VIA TEAMS OR EMAIL

 * Send an internal email by clicking Email in the Activities section.
 * If immediate attention is required, initiate a Microsoft Teams chat with the
   assigned agent or team.


STEP 5: MONITOR STATUS & CLOSE INTERNAL TASK

 * Review the case status and activity updates.
 * Once internal feedback is received, close the task and proceed with external
   follow-up.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. CUSTOMER CASE FOLLOW-UP


STEP 1: CHECK CASE PROGRESS

 * Open the Case Record and review the Case Timeline.
 * Identify pending actions or updates.


STEP 2: CHOOSE FOLLOW-UP METHOD

 * Email: Use email templates for consistency.
 * Phone Call: Log the details in Case Activities.
 * Live Chat: Update the customer in real-time (if using Omnichannel).


STEP 3: SEND AN UPDATE

 1. Click + Add Activity > Email within the Case.
 2. Select an Email Template or write a custom response.
 3. Include:
    * Case Number
    * Current Status
    * Next Steps & Expected Resolution Time
    * Customer Portal Link (if applicable)
 4. Click Send & Track Response.


STEP 4: LOG CUSTOMER RESPONSE

 * If the customer responds, update the case notes in the Timeline.
 * If additional action is required, create a Task or reassign the case.


STEP 5: SET A REMINDER FOR NEXT FOLLOW-UP

 * If no immediate resolution is available, create a follow-up task.
 * Mark the next follow-up date and notify the assigned agent.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


3. VENDOR CASE FOLLOW-UP

(Suitable for cases involving third-party vendors, suppliers, or service
providers.)


STEP 1: GATHER VENDOR CONTACT INFORMATION

 * Open the Case Record and check for linked vendor details.
 * If the vendor is not listed, locate the contact under Accounts or Contacts.


STEP 2: SEND A VENDOR INQUIRY

 * Click + Add Activity > Email and address it to the vendor contact.
 * Include:
   * Case Reference Number
   * Issue Summary
   * Required Action from the Vendor
   * Deadline for Response


STEP 3: FOLLOW-UP WITH A PHONE CALL (IF NEEDED)

 * If no response is received within the SLA, call the vendor.
 * Log the phone call under Activities > Phone Call.


STEP 4: UPDATE THE CASE RECORD

 * Document the vendor’s response and next steps in the Case Timeline.
 * If additional vendor actions are required, set a Follow-up Task.


STEP 5: NOTIFY THE CUSTOMER (IF APPLICABLE)

 * If the vendor provides a resolution, update the customer.
 * If delays occur, inform the customer with an expected timeline.

Description:
As a Customer Service Representative (CSR),

I want to merge duplicate cases into a single case,
So that I can avoid redundancy and improve case tracking.



STEPS TO MERGE CASES IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

In Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service, merging duplicate or related cases
ensures a streamlined case management process by consolidating information into
a single case record.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. WHEN TO MERGE CASES

Merging is useful when:
A customer submits multiple cases for the same issue.
Two agents create separate cases for the same customer request.
A case is mistakenly duplicated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. STEPS TO MERGE CASES IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE


STEP 1: OPEN THE CASE LIST VIEW

 1. Navigate to Service > Cases in D365.
 2. Identify the cases you want to merge.


STEP 2: SELECT CASES TO MERGE

 1. Select the primary case (the case that will remain).
 2. Select the secondary case(s) (the ones to be merged into the primary case).
 3. Click on the "Merge Cases" option in the command bar.


STEP 3: CONFIRM THE MERGE DETAILS

 1. A confirmation dialog will appear.
 2. Choose how to handle activities:
    * Keep activities and merge them into the primary case.
    * Close activities in the secondary case(s).
 3. Confirm that the selected primary case is correct.
 4. Click Merge.


STEP 4: VERIFY THE MERGED CASE

 1. Open the primary case.
 2. Ensure that:
    * Notes, emails, and activities from the secondary case(s) have been
      transferred.
    * The case status and owner remain unchanged.
 3. The merged cases are now marked as Canceled and linked in the Case Timeline.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


3. IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS



 * Merging is irreversible – verify case details before merging.
 * All activities from secondary cases will be linked to the primary case.
 * SLAs on the primary case remain active; merged cases lose their SLA tracking.
 * Security roles must allow merging cases.

STEPS TO SEND A KNOWLEDGE ARTICLE TO A CUSTOMER IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Sharing a Knowledge Article with a customer helps provide quick resolutions and
improve case efficiency. This guide outlines the steps to find, attach, and send
a Knowledge Article in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. WHEN TO SEND A KNOWLEDGE ARTICLE



 * The article contains troubleshooting steps relevant to the case.
 * The customer has a frequently asked question.
 * The issue can be resolved using self-help instructions.
 * The agent wants to provide additional reference material.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. STEPS TO SEND A KNOWLEDGE ARTICLE IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE


STEP 1: OPEN THE CASE RECORD

 1. Navigate to Service > Cases in D365.
 2. Select the case where you want to send an article.
 3. Open the case details page.


STEP 2: SEARCH FOR A KNOWLEDGE ARTICLE

 1. In the Case Form, locate the Knowledge Search pane (usually on the right
    side).
 2. Type relevant keywords related to the issue.
 3. Select the most appropriate Knowledge Article.
 4. Click Associate to link the article to the case.


STEP 3: SEND THE KNOWLEDGE ARTICLE TO THE CUSTOMER

OPTION 1: SEND VIA EMAIL

 1. Click Email a link or Attach to Email (based on your setup).
 2. A new email window will open with the article attached or linked.
 3. Personalize the email with:
    * Case Number
    * Customer Greeting
    * Brief Explanation of the Article
 4. Click Send.

Description:
As a Customer Service Agent,

I want to collaborate with my team using a case swarm,
So that I can resolve complex issues faster with expert input.





STEPS TO SWARM ON A CASE WITH A TEAM IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

A Case Swarm is a collaborative approach where multiple agents, teams, or
experts work together on a complex case to expedite resolution. In Microsoft
Dynamics 365 Customer Service, SWARMING ensures that difficult cases get the
attention they need from the right people.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. WHEN TO SWARM ON A CASE

The case is complex and requires input from multiple experts.
A high-priority or VIP customer case needs immediate resolution.
The assigned agent lacks the expertise to resolve the issue alone.
The issue spans multiple departments (e.g., IT, Billing, Customer Support).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. STEPS TO INITIATE A CASE SWARM IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE


STEP 1: IDENTIFY THE NEED FOR A SWARM

 * Open the Case Record and review the issue details.
 * Check if previous troubleshooting attempts were unsuccessful.
 * Determine the required expertise (technical support, billing, etc.).


STEP 2: START A SWARM DISCUSSION IN MICROSOFT TEAMS

 1. In the Case Record, click the "Collaborate" (Microsoft Teams
    Integration) button.
 2. Select Start a Teams Chat or Meeting with relevant agents.
 3. Tag subject matter experts and provide a brief case summary.
 4. Attach relevant case details, notes, or customer history.


STEP 3: ASSIGN TASKS TO TEAM MEMBERS

 * Within D365 Activities, create Tasks for each contributor.
 * Assign owners, set due dates, and track progress.
 * Use Power Automate to notify team members automatically.


STEP 4: UPDATE THE CASE WITH FINDINGS & NEXT STEPS

 * As each participant provides input, log updates in the Case Timeline.
 * Summarize key takeaways from the swarm session.
 * Assign follow-ups or escalation steps if needed.


STEP 5: COMMUNICATE WITH THE CUSTOMER

 * Once a resolution path is determined, update the customer.
 * If additional time is needed, provide an estimated resolution timeframe.
 * Send a Knowledge Article if applicable.


STEP 6: CLOSE THE SWARM & MONITOR CASE PROGRESS

 * Mark internal tasks as Completed once team contributions are finalized.
 * If resolved, close the case and request customer feedback.
 * If unresolved, escalate the case to higher support levels.

Title 4: Track additional information against a case
Description:
As a Customer Service Representative (CSR),

I want to attach documents, add notes, and create relationships between cases
and other records,
So that I can maintain a complete and organized case history for better
resolution tracking.





STEPS TO TRACK ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AGAINST A CASE IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

To ensure comprehensive case management, agents often need to attach documents,
add notes, update the timeline, and create relationships between cases or other
records in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service (D365 CE). This guide
outlines the steps to track and manage additional case-related
information efficiently.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. ACCESSING THE CASE IN CUSTOMER SERVICE WORKSPACE


STEP 1: OPEN THE CASE IN CUSTOMER SERVICE WORKSPACE

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Workspace in D365.
 2. Click on Cases from the left-hand navigation panel.
 3. Use the search bar or filters to find the case you need.
 4. Click on the case to open the record.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. ATTACHING DOCUMENTS TO A CASE


STEP 1: UPLOAD A FILE TO THE CASE TIMELINE

 1. In the Timeline section, click + Add Note.
 2. Type a brief description of the document.
 3. Click Attach File, select the file from your system, and click Upload.
 4. Click Save to link the document to the case.


STEP 2: UPLOAD TO SHAREPOINT (IF ENABLED)

 1. Scroll to the Documents section in the case form.
 2. Click Upload and select the file.
 3. The document is now stored in the linked SharePoint folder.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


3. UPDATING THE TIMELINE ON A CASE


STEP 1: ADD A NOTE TO THE TIMELINE

 1. In the Case Record, navigate to the Timeline section.
 2. Click + Add Note.
 3. Enter relevant case details, updates, or progress tracking.
 4. (Optional) Use the "@" symbol to mention a colleague for collaboration.
 5. Click Save – the note will now be visible in the Case Timeline.


STEP 2: LOG AN ACTIVITY (EMAIL, PHONE CALL, TASK, ETC.)

 1. In the Timeline, click + Add Activity.
 2. Choose the appropriate activity type (e.g., Phone Call, Email, Task).
 3. Enter the necessary details:
    * For Phone Calls: Log the conversation details.
    * For Emails: Compose and send an email directly from the case.
    * For Tasks: Assign follow-ups to agents.
 4. Click Save – the activity is now recorded in the Case Timeline.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


4. CREATING RELATIONSHIPS TO OTHER RECORDS OR CASES


STEP 1: LINK A CASE TO ANOTHER CASE (PARENT/CHILD RELATIONSHIP)

 1. Open the Case Record that will be the "Child" case.
 2. Scroll to the Related Cases section.
 3. Click + New Case Relationship.
 4. Select the Parent Case from existing records.
 5. Click Save & Close.

Use Case: When a case is related to a larger issue, linking it as a Child
Case allows tracking under one Parent Case.


STEP 2: LINK A CASE TO OTHER RECORDS (CONTACTS, ACCOUNTS, WORK ORDERS, ETC.)

 1. Open the Case Record.
 2. Navigate to the Related Records section.
 3. Select the type of record you want to link (e.g., Contacts, Accounts, Work
    Orders, Opportunities).
 4. Click + Add Existing Record or + New Record if it doesn’t exist.
 5. Click Save to establish the relationship.

Use Case: If a case is related to a specific customer account, asset, or work
order, linking ensures better traceability.


5. BEST PRACTICES



 * Use SharePoint Integration for secure and centralized document storage.
 * Keep Notes Organized by adding timestamps and tagging relevant agents.
 * Log All Interactions to maintain a full history of customer communications.
 * Automate Case Documentation – Use Power Automate to generate reports when a
   case is updated.

Description:
As a Customer Service Manager,

I want to analyze case patterns and trends,
So that I can identify recurring issues, optimize case resolution, and improve
customer satisfaction.



STEPS TO ANALYZE CASE PATTERNS IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Analyzing case patterns in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service helps
identify recurring issues, optimize resource allocation, and improve service
efficiency. This guide outlines how to use Customer Service Historical
Analytics to uncover case trends and patterns.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. ACCESSING CASE ANALYTICS IN D365


STEP 1: OPEN CUSTOMER SERVICE HISTORICAL ANALYTICS

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Workspace or Customer Service Hub.
 2. Click Customer Service Historical Analytics from the left-hand navigation
    panel.
 3. Open the Case Insights Dashboard.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. IDENTIFYING CASE TRENDS & RECURRING ISSUES


STEP 2: REVIEW CASE VOLUME TRENDS

Metrics to Analyze:

 * Total Cases Created Over Time – Identify seasonal or recurring spikes.
 * Case Volume by Type – Determine which types of issues occur most often.
 * Case Volume by Channel – Compare issues reported via email, chat, phone, or
   self-service portal.
 * Top Customers by Case Count – Identify customers submitting frequent cases.

Best Practice: Apply date range filters (weekly, monthly, quarterly) to spot
long-term trends.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 3: ANALYZE CASE RESOLUTION & ESCALATIONS

Key Metrics:

 * Average Resolution Time – Identify case types taking longer to resolve.
 * Escalation Rate by Case Type – Find case categories that frequently require
   higher-level intervention.
 * Case Reopen Rate – Detect cases that were closed but needed follow-up.

Best Practice: If certain case types have high escalation or reopen rates, they
may require process improvements or updated Knowledge Articles.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


3. ANALYZING AGENT & TEAM CASE HANDLING PATTERNS


STEP 4: EVALUATE AGENT & TEAM PERFORMANCE

 1. In Customer Service Historical Analytics, open the Agent Insights dashboard.
 2. Filter by Agent Name or Team.
 3. Analyze the following KPIs:
    * Average Case Handling Time Per Agent – Identify efficiency gaps.
    * Number of Cases Assigned vs. Resolved – Compare workload vs. output.
    * Escalation Rate Per Agent – Find agents frequently escalating cases.

Best Practice: Compare case resolution trends across different teams or
shifts to optimize staffing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


4. DETECTING SLA VIOLATIONS & RESOLUTION DELAYS


STEP 5: IDENTIFY SLA COMPLIANCE TRENDS

Key Metrics:

 * Total SLA Breaches – Cases exceeding response or resolution deadlines.
 * Cases Nearing SLA Deadline – Identify cases at risk of violating SLAs.
 * Case Resolution Time vs. SLA Goal – Compare actual vs. expected resolution
   performance.

Best Practice: Use Power Automate to notify managers when cases are approaching
SLA limits.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


5. LEVERAGING CUSTOMER FEEDBACK FOR PATTERN ANALYSIS


STEP 6: REVIEW CUSTOMER SATISFACTION (CSAT) SCORES

 1. Navigate to the CSAT (Customer Satisfaction) Dashboard.
 2. Analyze feedback on resolved cases.
 3. Identify recurring themes in low-rated cases (e.g., long wait times,
    incomplete resolutions).

Best Practice: If certain case types consistently get low ratings,
investigate process bottlenecks or training needs.


6. BEST PRACTICES FOR CASE PATTERN ANALYSIS

Monitor trends weekly/monthly to detect emerging issues early.
Use AI-powered insights (Copilot) to recommend case resolutions.
Optimize Knowledge Articles based on case trends.
Automate alerts for SLA risks and escalation trends with Power Automate.

Description:
As a Knowledge Manager,

I want to analyze how agents and customers use the Knowledge Base,
So that I can improve content quality and ensure articles help resolve cases.



STEPS TO ANALYZE KNOWLEDGE BASE USAGE IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Analyzing Knowledge Base (KB) usage in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer
Service helps organizations evaluate how effectively agents and customers are
using articles to resolve cases. This guide outlines the steps to track, review,
and optimize KB usage.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. WHY ANALYZE KNOWLEDGE BASE USAGE?

Identify the most frequently used articles.
Assess whether KB articles are resolving cases.
Determine gaps in knowledge content.
Improve article quality and relevance.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. STEPS TO ANALYZE KNOWLEDGE BASE USAGE IN D365


STEP 1: ACCESS KNOWLEDGE BASE INSIGHTS

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Hub or Customer Service Workspace.
 2. Click on Knowledge Articles in the left-hand navigation panel.
 3. Select Knowledge Search Analytics under Insights (if enabled).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 2: REVIEW KNOWLEDGE SEARCH ANALYTICS

Metrics to Analyze:

 * Top-searched keywords: Identify what agents and customers search for.
 * Most-viewed articles: See which articles are frequently accessed.
 * Article success rate: Review how often an article is linked to resolved
   cases.
 * Unused or low-performing articles: Identify articles that need updates or
   removal.

How to View Data:

 * Open Dashboards > Knowledge Search Analytics for graphical reports.
 * Use Power BI Reports if custom analytics are set up.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 3: TRACK KNOWLEDGE BASE USAGE IN CASES

 1. Open Service > Cases.
 2. Use the Knowledge Search panel to see linked articles.
 3. Filter cases by Knowledge Article Associations to check:
    * How often articles are attached to cases.
    * Whether articles contribute to case resolution.
    * Feedback on article effectiveness.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 4: ANALYZE AGENT ENGAGEMENT WITH KB ARTICLES

Navigate to Settings > Service Management > Knowledge Search Analytics.
Review:

 * Which agents use KB articles the most.
 * Article attachment trends per agent/team.
 * Cases where no KB article was used (indicating potential content gaps).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 5: GATHER CUSTOMER FEEDBACK ON KB ARTICLES

 1. Enable Knowledge Article Ratings & Feedback
    
    * Go to Settings > Service Management > Knowledge Settings.
    * Enable Ratings & Comments for KB articles.

 2. Review Customer Feedback
    
    * Open Knowledge Articles > Select an article.
    * View Ratings, Comments, and Helpful/Not Helpful votes.
    * Identify articles with poor feedback and update them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 6: USE REPORTS & DASHBOARDS FOR KB INSIGHTS

Standard Reports:

 * Open Reports > Knowledge Base Usage Report.
 * Export data to Excel for further analysis.

Power BI Dashboards (If Enabled):

 * Track Knowledge Base adoption trends.
 * Visualize article effectiveness per category or product.

Tracking call center performance, individual agent performance, and SLA (Service
Level Agreement) compliance ensures efficient customer service operations. This
guide outlines how to review and analyze these metrics using Microsoft Dynamics
365 Customer Service Historical Analytics.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. REVIEWING CALL CENTER PERFORMANCE BY CASE TYPE


STEP 1: ACCESS CUSTOMER SERVICE HISTORICAL ANALYTICS

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Workspace or Customer Service Hub.
 2. Click on Customer Service Historical Analytics from the left-hand navigation
    panel.
 3. Open the Case Insights Dashboard.


STEP 2: FILTER CASES BY TYPE

 1. Locate the Case Type field in the analytics dashboard.
 2. Use filters to categorize cases by type (e.g., Technical Issue, Billing,
    Warranty, Product Inquiry).
 3. Apply date filters to analyze performance over a specific period.


STEP 3: ANALYZE CASE TRENDS

Key Metrics to Review:

 * Total number of cases per type (Identify the most common issues).
 * Average resolution time by case type (Compare how quickly different case
   types are resolved).
 * First Contact Resolution (FCR) rate (How often cases are resolved in the
   first interaction).
 * Escalation rates by case type (Which types require managerial intervention).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. ANALYZING INDIVIDUAL AGENT PERFORMANCE


STEP 1: OPEN AGENT PERFORMANCE DASHBOARD

 1. In Customer Service Historical Analytics, go to Agent Insights.
 2. Select the Agent Performance dashboard.


STEP 2: REVIEW KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIS)



 * Total Cases Handled: Number of cases an agent has worked on.
 * Average Handling Time (AHT): The time taken to resolve cases.
 * Resolution Rate: Percentage of cases resolved by the agent.
 * Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT): Based on customer feedback and surveys.
 * Escalation Rate: Percentage of cases escalated to supervisors.




STEP 3: COMPARE AGENT PERFORMANCE

 * Filter by agent name to compare performance.
 * Identify top-performing agents vs. those needing training.
 * Check if agents handle certain case types more efficiently.

Best Practice: Use Power Automate to send automated alerts if an agent’s
performance drops below a set threshold.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1: ACCESS SLA COMPLIANCE DASHBOARD

 1. In Customer Service Historical Analytics, click on SLA Insights.
 2. Open the SLA Compliance dashboard.


STEP 2: IDENTIFY SLA BREACHES

Key Metrics to Analyze:

 * Total SLA violations (Number of missed SLAs).
 * Cases with SLA breaches (Filter cases that exceeded response/resolution
   time).
 * Agents with the highest SLA violations (Identify recurring issues).
 * SLA compliance percentage (Measure overall adherence).


STEP 3: DRILL DOWN INTO SLA VIOLATIONS

 * Filter by Case Type to see which case types frequently exceed SLA limits.
 * Filter by Agent/Team to identify who is missing SLAs.
 * Review SLA breach reasons (e.g., long wait times, agent workload).

Best Practice: Automate SLA alerts in Power Automate to notify managers when an
SLA is about to breach.




4. Best Practices for Call Center Performance Management



 * Use AI-powered insights (Copilot for Customer Service) for real-time
   analytics.
 * Enable SLA breach notifications in Power Automate.
 * Regularly review performance dashboards to address gaps proactively.
 * Use Power BI for deeper analytics beyond built-in reports.
