Title 4: Review case loads and rebalance case loads
Description:
As a Customer Service Manager,

I want to analyze and redistribute case loads across my team,
So that no agent is overwhelmed and cases are resolved efficiently.



STEPS TO REVIEW AND REBALANCE CASE LOADS IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE

Effectively reviewing and rebalancing case loads ensures that agents are not
overwhelmed and that cases are resolved efficiently. This guide outlines how to
analyze case distribution and redistribute cases using Microsoft Dynamics 365
Customer Service Historical Analytics.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


1. REVIEWING CASE LOADS IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE


STEP 1: ACCESS CUSTOMER SERVICE HISTORICAL ANALYTICS

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Workspace or Customer Service Hub.
 2. Click on Customer Service Historical Analytics from the left-hand navigation
    panel.
 3. Open the Agent Insights Dashboard or Case Insights Dashboard.


STEP 2: REVIEW CURRENT CASE LOAD DISTRIBUTION

Key Metrics to Analyze:

 * Total Cases Assigned Per Agent: Identify overloaded agents.
 * Active vs. Resolved Cases: Determine backlog levels.
 * Case Aging Report: Find cases that have been open too long.
 * Escalation Rate Per Agent: Identify performance gaps.
 * SLA Status by Agent: Check if any agents are at risk of breaching SLAs.


STEP 3: IDENTIFY IMBALANCES IN CASE LOADS

 * Compare case volumes across different agents and teams.
 * Look for agents with a significantly higher number of open cases.
 * Identify unassigned or overdue cases that require reassignment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


2. REBALANCING CASE LOADS IN D365 CUSTOMER SERVICE


STEP 1: REASSIGN CASES MANUALLY

 1. Navigate to Customer Service Workspace and open Cases.
 2. Use filters to identify:
    * Overloaded agents.
    * Cases that need reassignment based on priority.
    * Unassigned cases that need a responsible owner.
 3. Select cases that need reassignment.
 4. Click Assign, then select the appropriate agent or team.
 5. Click Save to confirm the reassignment.

Best Practice: Leave an internal Case Note explaining why the case was
reassigned.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 2: AUTOMATE CASE BALANCING WITH QUEUES & ROUTING RULES

 1. Go to Service Management > Queues.
 2. Review the existing queues and ensure cases are evenly distributed.
 3. Navigate to Service Management > Routing Rules.
 4. Set up Auto-Assignment Rules based on:
    * Agent workload.
    * Case priority.
    * Case type and required expertise.

Best Practice: Use Omnichannel for Customer Service with Workstreams for
automatic case distribution.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEP 3: SET UP REAL-TIME ALERTS FOR CASE LOAD MONITORING



 * Use Power Automate to notify managers when:
 * An agent has more than a predefined number of active cases.
 * A case has been unassigned for too long.
 * An agent is consistently missing SLAs.




3. BEST PRACTICES FOR CASE LOAD BALANCING



 * Regularly review workload distribution to avoid agent burnout.
 * Use AI-based routing in Omnichannel for Customer Service for smarter case
   assignments.
 * Enable workload-based case reassignment in Power Automate.
 * Monitor SLA trends to prevent bottlenecks in case resolution.

Concept to market is the process of managing a service offering from its
inception to its eventual end of life. The process typically begins with the
development of a service offering idea, which is then refined and tested to
ensure that it meets customer needs. After the service is launched, it's
important to monitor its performance and make necessary adjustments to keep it
competitive in the marketplace. As the service offering matures, it might be
necessary to update or refresh the design to maintain customer interest.
Eventually, the service offering might reach the end of its marketable life and
be retired from the market. Throughout the concept to market process, careful
attention must be paid to customer needs, market trends, and technological
advancements to ensure that the service offering remains relevant and
successful.




In service-based organizations or organizations that sell services alongside
tangible products, Dynamics 365 offers a variety of products to help support the
design and development of new service offerings and control the downstream
transactions that occur in the organization. For example, when you use Dynamics
365 Field Service, you can define service offerings that are sold by using
Dynamics 365 Sales or Supply Chain Management. For complex services, such as
professional services, you can define the services in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain
Management or Sales, and use Dynamics 365 Project Operations to help manage the
lifecycle of your customer relationship. Additionally, you can mix and match
services with tangible products on orders, include services in your production
process, or outsource services by using Procurement and sourcing, Project
Operations, or Field Service, to give just a few examples.



Important: The process that is defined here doesn't include the process for
designing tangible products. Learn more at Design to retire introduction.


Every organization has variations of the concept to market process. Here, we
define the basic outline for any organization that is looking to implement a
technology solution to support the concept to market process for services.

Description: Media types classify the communication media used for sales and marketing campaigns. Marketing administrators create values that reflect the channels the organization actually plans and reports on, such as email, telephone, print, events, or another governed medium. Give each type a clear name and description, distinguish media from campaign groups and target audiences, and avoid duplicate values that differ only in spelling or team terminology. A stable media vocabulary helps campaign planners describe execution consistently and enables meaningful comparison of activity, cost, response, and effectiveness where related reporting uses the classification. Review historical campaigns before renaming or retiring a value so prior results remain interpretable. Validate the list with campaign owners and reporting stakeholders before broad use. Questions to ask include which media distinctions influence planning or performance analysis, how emerging channels are governed, and who decides when two media should be reported separately. Listen for indicators such as free-text channel names, duplicated media categories, campaigns assigned to a generic catch-all, inconsistent terminology across teams, or reports that cannot compare results by communication medium. Owner mapping requires review before publication.

Description:
Design to retire is the process of managing a product from its inception to its
eventual end of life. The process typically begins with the development of a
product offering idea, which is then refined and tested to ensure that it meets
customer needs. After the product is launched, it's important to monitor its
performance and make necessary adjustments to keep it competitive in the
marketplace. As the product matures, you might want to update or refresh the
design to maintain customer interest. Eventually, the product reaches the end of
its useful life, and you retire it from the market. Throughout this process,
product management requires careful attention to customer needs, market trends,
and technological advancements to ensure that the product remains relevant and
successful.




For the engineering-type products that are common in the manufacturing industry,
the product and lifecycle management process can involve managing complex bills
of materials (BOMs) or formulas. A BOM or formula lists all the parts and
components that go into a product, and their relationships to each other.
Management of a BOM requires careful attention to ensure that all components are
available in the correct quantities, and that account lead times, availability,
and cost are also considered. Some organizations offer products that are
variable or configurable. In such cases, you can use the product configurator in
Dynamics 365 to enable customers to select specific features and options for a
product. The options that a customer can choose from are dynamically updated and
control the BOM.



For retail organizations, the design to retire process often also involves
merchandising. Merchandising is the process of selecting and presenting products
to customers in a way that maximizes sales. It might include designing product
packaging, creating promotional materials, and managing inventory levels to
ensure that products are available when customers want them. Dynamics 365
Commerce includes several capabilities that help support the process of
enhancing product information with attributes, categorizing products for easy
navigation on a website, and relating products to each other. Examples include
up-selling and cross-selling of products, and the use of AI to suggest products
based on an analysis of products that other customers purchased. Effective
product and lifecycle management requires collaboration among multiple teams,
including engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and sales, to ensure that the
product is successful throughout its lifecycle.



Important: The process that is defined here doesn't include the process for
designing production routes. Learn more about that process at Plan to produce
introduction.


Every organization has variations of the design to retire process. Here, we
define the basic outline for any organization that is looking to implement a
technology solution to support the design to retire process.

Description:
All organizations group and categorize or segment their products into logical
grouping for various reasons. Dynamics 365 includes several capabilities that
you can consider implementing together at the beginning of a project. The terms
categorization, merchandising, and segmentation of products and services are all
related concepts. Although all three terms are often used interchangeably, they
do have distinct meanings and functions in the system as well. The following
list outlines the differences:- Categorization refers to the process for
grouping products or services based on shared characteristics.


 * Segmentation refers to the process of dividing a market (of typically
   customers) into smaller groups (or segments) based on shared characteristics
   or interests.
 * Merchandising refers to the process of presenting products or services in an
   appealing and attractive way to the customers.

It's important for an organization to consider carefully how it categorizes,
segments, and merchandises the products and services it offers. During the
implementation of a business solution, an organization often already has a way
of doing this already. It's important to consider if the current mechanism for
categorizing products and services meets all the business requirements, because
the implementation of a new technology solution is often a good time to consider
making a change. The organization might want to consider questions such as the
following list:

 * How do you drive downstream business processes and automation?
 * How do you report and analyze your data including operational reporting and
   financial reporting?
 * How has your business grown since the original mechanism of categorization,
   segmentation, or merchandising was developed?
 * How do you anticipate your business will grow in the future?

The answers to these questions should help inform your process for defining the
way you implement a technology solution to support the categorization of
products and services. This business process area should always be considered
early in a Dynamics 365 implementation project. Also consider the number of
changes that might be happening to the data in this area as well. This can make
integrations, data migration, and other aspects of your project more complex.



When an organization starts a Dynamics 365 implementation, it's important to
carefully consider how you define the product lines in the system. This includes
tasks like setting up item groups and product categories in Dynamics 365 Supply
Chain Management and product families in Dynamics 365 Sales. The business
process areas for categorizing either products or services also include the
definition of product policies. We recommend that you group similar items
together based on the expected behaviors they need in the system. This includes
settings like item model groups, reservations, storage, and tracking dimensions,
and more in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management.



Also, if your organization offers multiple types of products or services, you
should define the rules and configurations for each type of product or service
that you offer. For example, in the chemical or food and beverage industry, you
might use catch weight items. In some industries, consigned inventory is common
and requires more setup, configuration, and considerations. Similarly, the
service industry has considerations to make for the services that they offer,
including warranties, installation, and so on. Many organizations also charge
extra fees or service charges for tangible items that are sold which might
require more considerations. Dynamics 356 supports various flexible
configurations to support many types of products, services, and extra fees and
charges that might be charges to customers or imposed by suppliers.



Once you have a basic definition for organizing products or services, you can
categorize and build hierarchical structures and catalogs or assortments for the
downstream processes. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and Commerce support
multiple flexible hierarchies for procurement, sales, channel management, and
more. In Dynamics 365 Sales, you can create hierarchies of products or services
with product families. Dynamics 365 Commerce uses assortments to define product
mix for a retail channel such as the call center, retail store, or online store.
One or more assortments are then combined and assigned to a catalog for each
retail channel. This process often uses product attributes that further describe
the product. However, attributes can describe categories or retail channels as
well, for example.



When you group common or similar items together into categories, you can more
easily manage the attributes. Attributes serve an important function in
merchandising and for customers to find products that meet their requirements.
Attributes can be easily added at any time, but starting with a good baseline
for your project to help you meet reporting requirements is critical to
downstream analytics. With tools to mass update attribute values, you can easily
manage the values at any time and adapt to the changing customer needs and
supply chain.



With Dynamics 365 Customer Service, you can create and manage subjects to manage
complex hierarchies that can represent products, brands, or types of issues that
are reported by your customers, for example. With Dynamics 365 Customer
Insights, segments help you organize customers into groups based on their buying
habits and one common segment is typically related to the products customers
purchase. However, organizations can define many segments based on many
different attributes of the products that are purchased.

Title 6: Configure and maintain product information management parameters in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Product information management parameters govern shared product behavior and product-data presentation across product creation, release, configuration, attributes, and integrations. Implementation teams configure them when the organization needs consistent handling of product numbers, translations, default-order-quantity validation, configuration-model version behavior, and product-attribute integration scope.

The behavior domains include general product-number display and quantity validation, language fallback for product information, constraint-based configuration-model controls, product and item number-sequence ownership, shared numbering, and product-attribute integration settings. Treat these as policy groups rather than independent conveniences because together they shape how products are created, identified, displayed, validated, and exchanged.

Before configuration, establish product-master ownership, supported languages, product and item numbering strategy, configuration technology, category hierarchies, and any legal entity used as the master source for product identifiers. Determine default precedence between shared definitions, legal-entity released-product data, category inheritance, and product-level overrides. Business owners for product data, supply chain, Commerce, and integrations should approve the policy.

The settings affect product and service creation, product-owner and attribute processes, catalog categories, product release, imports, variant configuration, and identifier export. Validate manual and imported product creation, numbering, translated display, default-order-quantity behavior, configuration versions, and attribute synchronization. Review changes cross-functionally and regression-test every affected domain because a parameter change can alter identifiers, user presentation, validations, and integration payloads. The local graph confirms this deliverable as a hard prerequisite for multiple product-management scenarios. Use the captured Product information management parameters page to maintain configuration within inspected controls. Captured controls include: Save. Captured tabs include: General, Constraint-Based product configuration models, Number sequences, Shared number sequences, Product attributes.

Title 6: Configure and maintain batch attribute groups in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Batch attribute groups collect related batch attributes so they can be assigned and maintained as a reusable set instead of one characteristic at a time. They are useful when the same quality, composition, or condition characteristics apply to multiple batch-controlled products or customer-specific product requirements.

Before configuration, define the individual batch attributes, including their value types and any supported ranges, targets, increments, or tolerance behavior. Establish a controlled group name and description, decide which attributes belong together, and confirm that the products that will receive the group use an active batch tracking dimension. Use the Where used inquiry before changing established groups so the impact on assigned products is understood.

The group is consumed when batch attributes are associated with products and subsequently populated on inventory batches; those values can then support batch searches and reservations. Validate a group by assigning it to a representative batch-controlled product, recording batch values, and confirming that the intended attributes are available during batch inquiry or reservation. Govern additions, removals, and reused group membership because changes can affect quality capture, customer-specific requirements, batch selection, and the interpretation of historical batch data. Title 6: Configure and maintain dual use certificates in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Dual-use certificates record the authorization that applies to a dual-use released item for a destination country or region during a defined validity period. They support export-control review and can provide certificate numbers for sales orders, packing slips, and invoices.

Configure dual-use categories, mark the relevant released products as dual use, and define which destination countries require certificates before creating records. For each certificate, select the item and country or region, maintain the certificate number and effective and expiration dates, and choose the documents on which the number should print. Assign ownership for renewal and evidence retention. This setup is part of the simpler dual-use feature and is superseded where advanced export management jurisdictions are enabled.

Certificates are checked when users confirm a sales order containing a dual-use product for a destination that requires certification. If no valid certificate covers the confirmed ship date, the system warns the user. Validate a certificate with in-period, expired, and missing-certificate order confirmations and review the selected document outputs. Monitor expiry and update records when products, destinations, regulations, or certificate terms change so export warnings and printed information remain accurate. Use the captured Dual Use Certificates page to maintain configuration within inspected controls. Captured controls include: New, Delete, Save.

The association distinguishes a product, procurement, sales, retail, or other hierarchy role from the hierarchy's node structure itself and lets consuming processes find the correct category tree.

For each association, select the category hierarchy type and the hierarchy that should serve it, and confirm that the hierarchy's design matches the intended process. Treat the association as shared governance: avoid assigning a hierarchy merely because its labels look similar, and coordinate role changes with product-data, procurement, sales, commerce, and reporting owners that depend on category semantics.

Role associations are consumed when processes resolve the hierarchy for product categorization, category attributes, procurement categories, or category-based views and policies. Validate an association in its intended process by confirming that users see the expected hierarchy and can select the correct category node for a representative product or transaction. Review changes when hierarchy ownership or category strategy changes because redirecting a role can expose a different tree and alter downstream assignments and reporting. Use the captured Category hierarchy role associations page to maintain configuration within inspected controls. Captured controls include: New, Delete, Save.

Description:
The ability for an organization to create new products in their offerings plays
a pivotal role in the growth and innovation of the organization. The business
process area involves strategic development, launch and integration of fresh
offerings into the market, ensuring that the organization remains competitive
and responsive to the evolving customers' needs.




The process of introducing new offerings into the market can vary drastically
from industry to industry and geography to geography, among other factors.
However, one thing that is certain among all organizations, is that the process
can be costly, time consuming, and has a direct impact on the organization's
bottom line. For this reason, having strong technology solutions like Dynamics
365, Microsoft 365, and the Power Platform are essential to ensure that business
decision makers have the right information to make the right decisions.



Organizations can diversify their portfolio, tap into new revenue streams, and
strengthen market presence by introducing new products. The Dynamics 365 product
suite offers a variety of tools and products to help support this process and
products across multiple industries.



For example, Dynamics 365 Customer Service offers capabilities to support
tangible products that are offered to customers. Dynamics 365 Commerce offers
the capabilities to track sales in the point of sale, online, in a call center,
or with integrations from Dynamics 365 Sales or other third-party solutions that
help you manage your sales cycle. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management supports
the product lifecycle of manufactured products, distributed products, and much
more.



With complex support for various types of products across the portfolio, it's
important to select the right technologies to support your business needs. When
introducing new products, it's important to consider that careful execution of
the market research, ideation, rigorous testing, and seamless coordination
across departments is executed well.



Dynamics 365 Marketing offers tools to help with many steps, and when used
alongside our productivity tools like Microsoft Teams, Planner, and Outlook, and
Dynamics 365 Customer Voice, as a few examples, organization can successfully
implement solutions to support the process leading to increased customer
satisfaction, increased brand reputation, and sustainable growth.



When organizations are looking to implement technological solutions to support
the introduction of new products business process, we recommend that these
activities are prioritized and planned early in the process. The product data
that is captured as part of the business process is critical to many of the
downstream processes and poor implementation can cause data quality issues which
can lead to other issues later in the project and in the overall business cycle.
Keep in mind that product data is considered master data and should be carefully
planned and integrated into all downstream business processes.



If you are planning to use a third-party solution for product master data, you
can integrate your solution in the first phases of your product and you can look
to replace the third-party solution in a later phase. However, careful
considerations for the functionality needed should be taken early in the project
to avoid reworking later.

Title 6: Configure and maintain colors in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Colors define the reusable color dimension values used to identify product variants. They provide the global vocabulary from which color groups and product-specific dimension assignments are built, and they can also carry display, filter, and media properties for supported Commerce experiences.

Before configuration, agree on a stable identifier and naming policy that avoids duplicate values for the same business color. Determine global display order, translations, and any supported refiner, media, or visual representation requirements. Colors are product dimensions rather than descriptive attributes: use them when the value must participate in variant identity and transaction selection, and use attributes for characteristics that do not define a distinct product variant.

Color values are consumed when product variants are generated and selected on order, production, inventory, and other transaction lines. Their translated names can flow into variant names and external documents. Validate each value by associating it through the intended product master or color group, generating a representative variant, and confirming selection and translated display. Review renames or consolidation carefully because existing variants and transactions retain the dimension identity and inconsistent values can fragment search, assortment, reporting, and integration data. Use the captured Colors page to maintain configuration within inspected controls. Captured controls include: New, Delete, Save, Define media template.

Title 6: Configure and maintain color groups in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Color groups define curated sets of color dimension values that can be reused by product masters and product categories. They help organizations control which colors are available for a class of products and manage display, translation, replenishment, barcode, filtering, and media-related properties at the group-line level.

Before configuration, establish the global color values and a naming convention for groups that reflects stable assortments rather than individual products. Decide the membership and display order, maintain user-facing names and descriptions, and add translations needed for documents or channels. Where Commerce behavior applies, align barcode numbering, refiners, media templates, and replenishment weights with the merchandising design. Create variant groups before assigning them to products.

Color-group membership is consumed when product variants are generated and when translated dimension values contribute to variant names and external documents. The local deliverable graph also identifies color groups as a prerequisite for a production-estimate scenario whose bill of materials references color. Validate a group by assigning it to a representative product master, generating only intended variants, and checking order entry, translations, and any channel presentation. Govern membership and ordering changes because they can affect variant availability, planning, production estimates, barcodes, and merchandising output. Use the captured Color groups page to maintain configuration within inspected controls. Captured controls include: Back, Save, New, Delete, Copy, Personalize this page, Advanced filter or sort, Record info. Captured tabs include: Color group lines.

Title 6: Configure and maintain product relationship types in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Product relationship types define the business meanings used to connect one product to another, such as an accessory, substitute, or complementary offering. They provide a controlled vocabulary for product relationships so product teams and consuming experiences interpret each connection consistently.

Before configuration, agree which relationship meanings the organization needs, who owns the list, and how names should be understood across languages and channels. Give each type a clear name, friendly name, and description, and avoid overlapping meanings that could make product associations ambiguous. Product definitions and the processes that publish or distribute product information should already be governed.

These values are selected when relationships are created between products and can influence how related offerings are presented in procurement or other product experiences. Validate a type by relating two representative products and confirming that users see the intended friendly label and explanation. Review additions, translations, and retired meanings through product-data governance because changing a widely used type can alter how existing relationships are interpreted across applications and integrations. Title 6: Configure and maintain warranty groups in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Warranty groups connect warrantable products with the warranty products that can be offered for them. Commerce and product administrators use the page before extended warranties are sold so point-of-sale users can be prompted with relevant coverage rather than an unrestricted list.

Create a clearly named group, maintain its description and lifecycle status, and associate the applicable warranty products and warrantable products on their dedicated tabs. Coordinate membership with product assortments, warranty terms, pricing, channels, and publishing practices. Validate by testing representative products in the intended sales channel and confirm that the expected warranty offer appears only while the group and products are active. Review groups when assortments or warranty offerings change.

Questions to ask include which products qualify for which coverage, how stores handle overlapping offers, and who approves publication or retirement. Listen for indicators such as associates searching manually for warranties, irrelevant prompts, eligible products receiving no offer, inactive coverage remaining available, or channel teams maintaining separate compatibility lists. Use the captured Warranty groups page to maintain configuration within inspected controls. Captured controls include: New, Delete, Edit. Title 6: Configure and maintain country of origin vendor certificates in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Country of origin vendor certificates record certificate identifiers issued for a vendor, released item, and destination country or region during a defined validity period. They help product compliance teams track origin-related certification commitments and decide where certificate numbers should be available on commercial documents.

Establish vendor accounts, released items, country and region codes, and the organization's certificate-issuance process before creating records. Maintain the certificate number, effective and expiration dates, and the intended invoice, packing-slip, or sales-order print options. Treat the observed required fields as environment evidence and coordinate ownership with procurement, product compliance, and document-reporting teams. Standard reports do not print these certificate numbers without an implementation extension.

Certificate records are referenced for the selected vendor, item, destination, and date range and can feed extended invoices, packing slips, or order confirmations when those reports have been designed to include them. Validate a certificate by checking an in-period and expired scenario and reviewing each extended document selected for printing. Review records before expiration and whenever vendors, items, destinations, certificate terms, or report extensions change to prevent missing or misleading certification information. Title 6: Configure and maintain dual use categories in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:

They provide a controlled list of full classification codes and their category, product-group, and regime components for product assignment and reporting.

Title 6: Configure and maintain material reporting lists in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Regulated products regional lists define named material-reporting lists for a country or region and, where required, a state or province. Organizations use them to organize jurisdiction-specific product compliance information and distinguish lists that are reportable from other regional product lists. The underlying page is captioned Material reporting lists, while the catalog title describes its product-compliance purpose.

Before configuration, identify the governing jurisdictions and the regulatory or internal reporting lists that the organization must maintain. Establish a unique list ID and clear description, select the applicable country or region and optional state or province, and determine whether the list is marked as reported. Assign ownership to the product compliance or regulatory team and avoid creating overlapping lists whose jurisdiction or purpose cannot be distinguished. Configure related product compliance records and item assignments separately; this page defines the regional list header rather than assigning every product.

The lists provide regional context for product compliance maintenance and downstream reporting or review of regulated product information. Validate each list by confirming its jurisdiction, reported status, and description match the approved compliance design, then test the related product-assignment or reporting process that consumes the list. Review the setup whenever regulations, reporting obligations, jurisdictions, product portfolios, or organizational compliance ownership change. Preserve identifiers used by historical compliance records and retire obsolete lists through controlled governance rather than repurposing them for a different jurisdiction. Title 6: Configure and maintain restricted products regional lists in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:

Determine whether state-level scope is required and coordinate related product safety data sheet validity rules where those controls are part of the compliance design. Keep ownership and evidence of regulatory interpretation outside the list description so configuration changes remain traceable.

The lists are consumed when products are associated with regional restrictions and compliance users review product applicability by jurisdiction. Validate a list by adding a representative product through the related Restricted products function and confirming that it appears under the intended country or state without affecting another jurisdiction. Title 6: Configure and maintain approved item groups in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:

Govern membership changes because adding or removing one released item can immediately change which customers may buy it. Title 6: Configure and maintain product entity identifier codes in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Product entity identifier codes define the identifier categories and codes used to consolidate product identifiers for export to external systems. They provide readable classifications for identifier types such as product, item, barcode, external, or other supported identifiers without replacing the identifiers maintained on the underlying product records.

Before configuration, select the legal entity that owns the global product master scope and the product category hierarchy used for synchronization. Confirm which identifier types target systems require, generate the available code types, and govern their names and descriptions so integrations interpret them consistently. Coordinate barcode setups and external-code classes because generated code types can depend on those definitions.

After code types are approved, the Create identifiers process populates the global product identifier table, and related identifier and scope data can be exported. Validate by generating codes, creating identifiers for a controlled product subset, and reconciling exported codes, scopes, and source identifiers. Schedule and monitor recurring creation only after the reconciliation succeeds. Review changes with product-data and integration owners because deleting or renaming a code type can exclude identifiers or change their meaning for receiving systems. Microsoft notes that this identifier export model has limited practical use and may change, so confirm target-system compatibility. Use the captured Product entity identifier codes page to maintain configuration within inspected controls. Captured controls include: New, Delete, Generate codes, Create identifiers.

Title 6: Review expedite codes in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description: Expedite codes classify the urgency assigned to an order or delivery decision. Sales and distribution administrators create a unique code and description for each approved priority, such as a high priority that should ship as soon as possible or a low priority that can follow normal scheduling. Users can apply the code on individual sales orders, and the same classification can support mode-of-delivery setup. Define each level with operationally meaningful criteria so customer service, warehouse, and transportation teams interpret urgency consistently. Avoid creating duplicate labels that do not lead to a different action, and protect high-priority choices from routine use. Validate representative orders and delivery modes to confirm that the code is available and understood by downstream teams. Questions to ask include what circumstances justify expedited handling, who may assign or override urgency, and how additional cost or capacity is approved. Listen for indicators such as rush requests communicated outside the system, every order marked urgent, inconsistent priority language, or warehouse teams unable to distinguish service commitments. Owner mapping requires review before publication.

Description:
Managing product pricing is a pivotal aspect of organizational success,
influencing profitability and competitive positioning. In today's dynamic
business landscape, effective product pricing requires a comprehensive approach,
and when using the suite of Dynamics 365 products organizations can achieve
these goals. From Dynamics 365 Commerce to Customer Service, Field Service,
Project Operations, Sales, and Supply Chain Management, these interconnected
tools provide a robust framework for optimizing product pricing strategies.




Dynamics 365 enables organizations to seamlessly align pricing structures with
market demands and competitive landscapes, fostering transparent relationships
with clients. The suite facilitates agile responses to dynamic market changes,
ensuring adaptability and strategic refinement to stay ahead. Specifically, in
Dynamics 365 Commerce, businesses can apply advanced pricing models for both
business to business (B2B) and business to consumer (B2C) scenarios, across
channels such as online, in store, and in the back office, enhancing their
merchandising strategies and delivering personalized pricing experiences to
diverse customer segments.



The process of managing product pricing involves a series of interconnected
business processes crucial for organizational efficiency. Beginning with the
definition of a robust product catalog and strategy, organizations can introduce
new products seamlessly, strategically positioning them in the market. The
management of product pricing involves meticulous determination of prices and
eligibility for discounts, ensuring offerings align with market demands.



Simultaneously, defining product costing becomes paramount for maintaining
profitability. The holistic approach extends to managing the entire product
lifecycle, from introduction to retirement, ensuring continuous refinement and
strategic adaptation. This integrated process within Dynamics 365 empowers
organizations to navigate the complexities of product pricing with agility and
foresight, contributing to sustained success.



In an organization focused on products, especially when downstream processes
such as procure to pay, prospect to quote, order to cash, plan to produce,
project to profit, case to resolution, service to cash, and/or record to report
are part of the Dynamics 365 implementation, early consideration of business
processes related to managing product pricing is essential.



The data and output of these processes impact various downstream operations and
defining them early in the project ensures overall project success. If Dynamics
365 won't serve as the system of record for product data, integrations to the
designated system should be considered early in the planning phase.

Title 6: Create and configure trade agreement journal names in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Trade agreement journal names define reusable journal categories for maintaining sales prices and discounts. Each name gives pricing administrators a consistent entry point and default relation for journals that create or update customer, item, group, or all-record trade agreement lines.

Create a controlled journal name and description for each distinct pricing-maintenance purpose, then select the appropriate default relation. Align names with pricing ownership, approval practices, and the trade agreement types used by the organization. Avoid duplicate names that obscure whether a journal is intended for base prices, line discounts, multiline discounts, or another governed pricing activity.

The names are selected when trade agreement journals are created and posted, after which valid agreement lines influence price and discount determination on sales transactions. Validate each name by creating a representative journal, confirming the expected relation defaults, posting approved lines, and testing price calculation within the intended effective dates and dimensions. Review journal names when pricing governance or trade agreement policy changes, because incorrect defaults can lead to misclassified or unintended pricing records. Owner mapping requires review before publication.

Description:
Management of the product lifecycle within an organization is of paramount
importance for businesses that deal with tangible products, whether they are
involved in buying, selling, distributing, or manufacturing. Strategic
orchestration of the product lifecycle ensures optimal efficiency,
cost-effectiveness, and customer satisfaction.




When organizations use Dynamics 365 to maintain product information, the system
plays a pivotal role by seamlessly integrating various products, such as
Dynamics 365 Customer Service, Sales, Field Service, Project Operations, and
Supply Chain Management. This comprehensive integration provides a unified
approach and enables organizations to streamline operations, enhance
collaboration, and make informed decisions throughout the entire product
lifecycle.



The process of managing a product's lifecycle involves several critical business
processes, each of which contributes to the overarching success of the data and
downstream process. These business processes include analyzing product margins
of products that are sold or produced. Many signals can come from upstream
processes in the case-to-resolution process. These processes send signals that
inventory should be removed, or that item usage should be restricted in sales,
procurement, production, or servicing operations.



For organizations that manufacture products, it's critical to ensure that you:

 * Define and document clear engineering policies.
 * Maintain accurate product versions and details.
 * Process the requested changes with rigor to ensure compliance with
   established policies and regulations.

Furthermore, the capability to seamlessly request, process, and retire a product
underscores the agility and adaptability that Dynamics 365 affords.



Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management includes robust product information
management capabilities that seamlessly integrate with other products in the
suite. Therefore, organizations can navigate the complexities of the product
lifecycle with precision and ensure sustained success and adaptability in the
dynamic business landscape.



The business processes for managing the product lifecycle in a Dynamics 365
implementation should be addressed in the early to mid-design and configuration
stages of the project.

Description:
The term forecast to plan typically describes a collection of business processes
that an organization implements to estimate demand and determine how much supply
is required to meet those demands. The term forecast means a prediction of
future events, typically sales. The plan is the organization's articulation and
refinement of the forecast to determine exactly what to buy and produce.




Note: For the purposes of this end-to-end process and related  business process,
we are primarily focused on forecasting and planning of products and services,
as opposed to general ledger budgeting and financial planning.


The forecast to plan business process is typically part of an organization's
larger efforts to buy and sell products or services. It's deeply related to all
of the other end-to-end business processes that inform the forecasting and
planning strategies. And then the execution of the plan supports the completion
of the other operational processes. The upstream or downstream relationship of
the forecast to plan business process to the other business processes is highly
dependent on the operational strategies of the business. Learn more at Solution
architecture design: Vision and strategies.



For example, in a make to order environment, the forecast to plan process is a
downstream process from forecast to plan. While in a make to stock environment,
it's an upstream process. Organizations may also use multiple operational
strategies, which is fully supported in Microsoft business apps.



The high-level strategy for forecast to plan processes should be planned at the
early phases of a larger ERP implementation. The design and decisions made about
this process have an impact on downstream processes including integrations, data
that must be migrated, and so on. If your organization doesn't have a
forecasting or planning process, or the forecast to plan approach is out of
scope for early phases of your project, add forecast to plan business processes
into your design later.



Important: The process defined here does not include the details for forecasting
and planning financials including cash flow forecast. Learn more at Record to
report introduction.


The process defined here also does not include the details for forecasting and
planning human resources. Learn more at Hire to retire introduction.



Every organization has variations to the forecast to plan processes. In this
article, we define the basic benefits and outcomes for any organization looking
to implement a technology solution to support the forecast to plan process.

future events, typically sales. The plan is the organization's articulation and
refinement of the forecast to determine exactly what to buy and produce.
Note: For the purposes of this end-to-end process and related  business process,
we are primarily focused on forecasting and planning of products and services,
as opposed to general ledger budgeting and financial planning. The forecast to
plan business process is typically part of an organization's larger efforts to
buy and sell products or services. It's deeply related to all of the other
end-to-end business processes that inform the forecasting and planning
strategies. And then the execution of the plan supports the completion of the
other operational processes. The upstream or downstream relationship of the
forecast to plan business process to the other business processes is highly
dependent on the operational strategies of the business. Learn more at Solution
architecture design: Vision and strategies. For example, in a make to order
environment, the forecast to plan process is a downstream process from forecast
to plan. While in a make to stock environment, it's an upstream process.
Organizations may also use multiple operational strategies, which is fully
supported in Microsoft business apps. The high-level strategy for forecast to
plan processes should be planned at the early phases of a larger ERP
implementation. The design and decisions made about this process have an impact
on downstream processes including integrations, data that must be migrated, and
so on. If your organization doesn't have a forecasting or planning process, or
the forecast to plan approach is out of scope for early phases of your project,
add forecast to plan business processes into your design later. Important: The
process defined here does not include the details for forecasting and planning
financials including cash flow forecast. Learn more at Record to report
introduction. The process defined here also does not include the details for
forecasting and planning human resources. Learn more at Hire to retire
introduction. Every organization has variations to the forecast to plan
processes. In this article, we define the basic benefits and outcomes for any
organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the forecast
to plan process.

Description:
The hire to retire process, also known as the employee lifecycle, is a critical
business process that involves various activities from recruiting and onboarding
employees to their separation from a company. In the context of Dynamics 365,
the hire to retire process is facilitated and streamlined using various HR
modules and tools available in the system.




A key portion of the process is defining your organizational structure and
planning and then recruiting your workforce. In this stage the organization
identifies its hiring needs, employee benefits, and compensation plans, and then
begins talent acquisition, the recruiting of qualified candidates. Dynamics 365
includes features to help managers request positions, to recruit, and to
streamline communications between departments. It also includes integration
capabilities to existing Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to help you integrate
your data into job boards and external sites.



Once a candidate is hired, the onboarding process begins. Dynamics 365 includes
onboarding features that help automate the onboarding process for new employees
and to help your internal teams to prepare for the new hire.



The next stage of the process is managing the employee lifecycle, which includes
performance management, career development, and succession planning. Dynamics
365 includes employee development capabilities such as the performance
management module that automates the performance appraisal process by enabling
managers to set goals, track progress, provide feedback, and conduct performance
reviews. The system also includes a Learning module that allows employees to
access training and development materials and track their progress towards
career goals. With the Learning Management System (LMS) APIs you can quickly and
easily surface the right courses to your workforce at the right time. HR
managers can use tools such as skill gap analysis to identify and develop
high-potential employees and create career development plans for them.



Dynamics 365 also includes tools to help with the day-to-day operations of the
organization including managing time, leave and absence, and expenses for your
workforce. For the HR team, we have features to help you stay compliant, perform
audits, track safety incidents, and more. And of course, Dynamics 365 enables
streamlined end-to-end integrations with partnering payroll systems via a
payroll integration API.



The final stage of the process is separation. Dynamics 365 includes a Benefits
management module that enables HR managers to manage employee benefits and
retirement plans, ensuring that retiring employees receive the benefits they are
entitled to. The system also includes features to help workers who are
transitioning (into new roles or management, for example) or offboarding that
helps to streamline the process of separating employees from the organization,
including the exit interview process and the collection of company property that
are tracked through loaned items.



The Microsoft 365 productivity suite can also be leveraged to help improve
collaboration and communication within teams and across organizations,
streamline business processes and workflows, enhance data security and
compliance, and increase overall productivity and efficiency. With its diverse
range of tools and applications such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive,
Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and more, Microsoft 365 offers a comprehensive
solution for businesses of all sizes to achieve their goals and objectives.
Other capabilities can be leveraged through use with tools such as Dynamics 365
Customer Voice, extension through the Power Platform, and integration with
products such as Power BI, Dynamics 365 Finance, and Dynamics 365 Supply Chain
Management.



Every organization has variations of the hire to retire process. Here, we define
the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology
solution to support the hire to retire process.

Description:
In today's dynamic business landscape, the implementation of occupational health
and safety processes is essential for maintaining a safe and productive work
environment. With Dynamics 365, organizations can streamline and enhance their
safety management processes. The defined processes can cover areas such as the
following list:

 * Hazard identification
 * Safety protocol documentation
 * Safety condition analysis
 * Safety audits
 * Staff training
 * Injury or illness reporting
 * Treatment seeking
 * Cost-of-care determination
 * Safety communication

These processes collectively contribute to a safer and healthier workplace. When
you use Dynamics 365 with Microsoft 365 products, such as Viva Learning or Viva
Engage, you can streamline business processes and improve your overall health
and safety metrics.



These processes serve a twofold purpose in any organization. First, they ensure
the well-being of employees, reducing the risk of workplace accidents and
health-related issues. Second, they help organizations meet legal and regulatory
requirements, avoid potential liabilities, and enhance their reputation as
responsible corporate citizens. Dynamics 365 implementations facilitate the
systematic execution of these processes, providing an efficient and centralized
platform for managing safety-related data, incidents, and compliance.



One notable advantage of implementing occupational health and safety processes
within Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 is their flexibility. None of these
processes are mandatory prerequisites for the system's operation, allowing
organizations to tailor their safety management to their specific needs and
timelines. These processes can be easily integrated into the system at any stage
of its operation or even incrementally added as the organization evolves. This
adaptability ensures that companies can respond to changing safety requirements,
growth, and new regulations without major disruptions to their operations. This
way, Dynamics 365 becomes a valuable tool for long-term safety and compliance
management.

Description:
Managing employee performance and growth is integral to the success of any
organization, serving as a cornerstone for fostering a motivated and skilled
workforce. In today's dynamic business landscape, Dynamics 365 plays a pivotal
role in streamlining this process.




Specifically, Dynamics 365 Human Resources and Customer Voice synergize to
provide a comprehensive solution. Dynamics 365 Human Resources facilitates the
definition of performance and review processes, competency requirements, career
paths, and learning plans. Meanwhile, Customer Voice helps in gathering valuable
feedback, contributing to a holistic view of employee performance. This
integration empowers organizations to align their workforce strategies with
real-time insights, ensuring a more effective approach to employee development.



When you use Dynamics 365 Human Resources together with Dynamics 365 Project
Operations, Supply Chain Management, or Field Service, you can manage the skills
required to perform work including project work, production work, or field work.
When you use Dynamics 365 Human Resources together with Dynamics 365 Commerce,
you can manage the shifts and training for the frontline workforce in a brick
and mortar or call center stores. Adding in Dynamics 365 Guides provides
augmented reality to help train and upskill employees while using Dynamics 365
Remote Assist can be used to assist field workers in their work to monitor or
upskill. While Dynamics 365 Customer Service includes features and ability to
integrate with telephony system to monitor calls and monitor the customer
service that is being delivered to customers.



Now, delving into the intricacies of managing employee performance and growth, a
series of interconnected business processes come into play. These processes
encompass defining performance and review procedures including the goal setting
process and documenting employee performance. Skill management is broken up into
several business process areas including establishing required competencies for
roles, maintaining a repository of skills and competencies, analyzing gaps
between skills required for the jobs to be done and the skills of the workforce.



The employee growth process including learning, and succession planning
containing process areas such managing course offerings, creating learning
plans, assigning courses, recording employee progress of assigned learning, and
analyzing/reporting on employee learning. These processes also include outlining
employee career paths and formulating succession plans. This comprehensive list
of processes is supported within Dynamics 365 and help organizations not only
automating but also optimizing the entire employee management lifecycle,
promoting efficiency and strategic decision-making for organizations aiming to
cultivate a high-performance culture.



The features and functionality for managing employee performance and growth
aren't mandatory to run Dynamics 365 Human Resources; any of the features can be
added at any time. Some downstream features such as skills competencies may be
required for downstream scheduling processes, for example, in Dynamics 365 Field
Service, Project Operations, and Supply Chain Management. In these cases, the
skill definition and management processes should be planned earlier in the
project to define the flow of data for the downstream processes.

Description:
Managing employee time and attendance is a critical aspect of organizational
efficiency, playing a pivotal role in ensuring optimal workforce productivity
and compliance. In today's dynamic business environment, the use of Dynamics 365
products, such as Human Resources, Project Operations, Field Service, and Supply
Chain Management, can help organizations streamline these crucial processes.
These tools enable an interconnected approach to time and attendance management
including leave and absence management, fostering a more cohesive and efficient
work environment.




The process of managing employee time and attendance encompasses several key
business processes that are supported by Dynamics 365. Organizations typically
start by defining and managing time and attendance policies to align with their
specific requirements. Dynamics 365 Human Resources supports flexible
configuration for leave and absence policies and plans including sick time, paid
time off, selling or borrowing leave, and the leave accrual process.



In addition, you can use Dynamics 365 Human Resources to record employee
absences and facilitate requests for time off, all seamlessly integrated into
the employee self-service experience. In addition, Dynamics 365 Commerce
supports the ability to create and managing shifts.



Depending on your industry and time-reporting needs, Dynamics 365 allows
employees to create and submit timesheets. This includes time clocks
functionality with Dynamics 365 Commerce, Human Resources, and Supply Chain
Management. For more complex manufacturing environments, you can use job card
terminals on the production floor or the Time and attendance module in Dynamics
365 Supply Chain Management, providing a comprehensive overview of their work
hours and production completed. Supervisors can then efficiently review and
approve timesheets, ensuring accuracy and compliance.



When you use Dynamics 365 Field Service or Project Operations, you can record
time against specific work orders or projects for detailed time reporting that
can be easily allocated to the right financial resources for billing, cost
recognition, and revenue recognition. The flexibility of the Dynamics 365
platform also allows for easy adjustments and corrections to timesheets,
ensuring that the time and attendance data remains accurate and reflective of
the dynamic nature of business operations.



Determining the high-level architecture of your solution early in the
implementation for your time and attendance business processes is important, but
you can leave the configuration and setup to the later stages of your project.

Description:
The inventory to deliver business process involves managing the flow of goods
from receipt into a warehouse or distribution center through to delivery to the
customer. This end-to-end process includes receipt of goods, quality management,
inventory management, inventory costing, order fulfillment, and shipping.




Important: The process defined here doesn't include the procurement process,
which involves purchasing raw materials or finished goods from suppliers. It
only includes the receipt of goods in the warehouse.
The process also doesn't include production, which involves converting raw
materials into sub-assemblies or finished goods. This process does include the
issuing of raw materials into production and the receipt of finished goods into
inventory.



Every organization has variations to the inventory to deliver process. Here, we
define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology
solution to support their inventory to deliver business processes.

Title 6: Create and configure auto cost in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Auto costs define rules that calculate and add expected landed costs automatically for voyages, shipping containers, folios, purchase orders, items, and transfer-order lines. They reduce manual charge entry and apply consistent cost policy according to the business context of each record.

Design the rule hierarchy by account, shipping company, mode of delivery, origin and destination ports, and effective dates. For each line, select the cost type, apportionment method, currency, value, minimum, tax treatment, and any linked cost. Confirm that prerequisite cost type codes, currencies, ports, carriers, and allocation policies are available, and govern overlapping rules so the intended rule is selected.

The rules are consumed when qualifying Landed cost records are created and costs are estimated or allocated. Validate representative combinations for each cost area, including boundary dates and exceptions, and confirm the correct cost, currency, apportionment, and accounting treatment is produced without duplicate charges. Review rules when carrier contracts, duty rates, routes, currencies, allocation policy, or effective periods change, because stale or overlapping rules can misstate inventory landed cost, accruals, margins, and voyage estimates.

Title 6: Create and configure cost template in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Cost templates define reusable defaults for estimating landed costs when the person requesting an estimate should not have to choose every costing option. A landed cost administrator maintains the templates in the Landed cost costing setup and aligns them with the organization’s approved estimation methods, currencies, cost types, and assumptions. The template reduces repeated selections and helps users produce comparable estimates for voyages or imported goods.

Use distinct templates where business units, routes, modes of transport, or estimation policies require materially different defaults. Validate each template with representative purchases and compare the estimate with the detailed cost assumptions before operational use. Changes should be governed because a revised default can alter later estimates without changing the underlying commercial agreement.

Questions to ask include which estimating decisions users can make, which assumptions must be standardized, and who approves exceptions. Listen for indicators such as inconsistent estimates, frequent manual overrides, unclear ownership of cost assumptions, or different practices by route and legal entity.

Title 6: Create and configure cost type code in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Cost type codes classify the charges that make up the landed cost of goods or a voyage, such as freight, duty, handling, and other adjustments. They determine how a charge is identified and support either capitalization into inventory value or accrual and clearing through the ledger.

Create a distinct code and description for each cost category, then define its posting treatment, including the clearing account and any ledger adjustments required by the accounting design. Coordinate the list with auto-cost rules, allocation methods, chart-of-accounts ownership, tax treatment, and financial reporting. Avoid duplicate codes with different posting intent, and document when a cost should increase inventory value versus be accrued or expensed.

Cost type codes are selected on manual and automatic voyage costs and flow through estimation, apportionment, receipt, invoice matching, and ledger posting. Validate each material code with a representative voyage or order, confirming the charge is allocated to the intended goods and posts to the expected inventory, expense, accrual, and clearing accounts. Review codes and posting setup when contracts, accounting policy, tax rules, or the chart of accounts changes, because incorrect treatment can distort inventory valuation and financial statements.

Title 6: Create and configure vendor cost type group in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Vendor cost type groups classify vendors that share similar landed-cost charge characteristics. A landed cost administrator uses the groups when automatic cost rules should apply consistently to a vendor population instead of being maintained vendor by vendor. For example, vendors operating in a market with a common duty treatment can be grouped when the same type of purchased product attracts the same charge policy.

Define groups around genuine cost-rule differences and give each group a name that procurement and logistics users can interpret. Coordinate assignments with vendor master data and the automatic cost setup, and avoid overlapping classifications that make rule selection ambiguous. Validate the design with representative vendors and voyages, confirming that the intended charges are found without affecting vendors outside the group.

Questions to ask include what vendor characteristics drive shared import costs, where exceptions occur, and who owns group assignment. Listen for indicators such as duplicated charge rules, regional duty differences, vendor reclassification, or unexpected voyage costs caused by broad group membership.

Title 6: Create and configure item over/under tolerance group in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Item over and under tolerance groups collect items that share acceptable receipt-quantity variance rules in Landed cost. Inventory or logistics administrators use the groups to maintain a common tolerance policy once and apply it consistently to similar items, rather than repeating the same limits item by item. The setup supports controlled handling of quantities received above or below the expected amount.

Define groups according to measurable business differences such as product characteristics, supplier practices, handling constraints, or regulatory controls. Assign items carefully, document who can approve exceptions, and avoid broad groups that hide materially different risk. Validate each group with representative over-receipt and under-receipt cases at and beyond the intended boundaries, confirming the operational response before rollout.

Questions to ask include what variance is commercially acceptable, which items require stricter control, and how exceptions are resolved. Listen for indicators such as frequent quantity disputes, variable bulk-material receipts, regulated products, manual overrides, or different tolerance ownership across warehouses and buying teams.

Title 6: Create and configure landed cost parameter in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:

Within the legal-entity Landed cost parameter design, determine the arrival grouping policy, default behavior, and ownership alongside the module’s general, validation, defaulting, status-update, voyage-creation, costing, inventory-dimension, and numbering settings. Keep the design aligned with receiving operations rather than treating it as an isolated lookup.

The configured behavior is used when voyage lines progress toward warehouse receipt and arrival registration. Validate it with a representative voyage containing the intended purchase or transfer lines, then confirm that arrival work is grouped as expected and can proceed through receiving without losing voyage traceability. Review the setting when warehouse operating models, inbound consolidation policy, voyage design, or receiving responsibilities change.

warehouse process where workers pick items for multiple orders simultaneously.
It involves grouping similar items together, often on a cart or tote, and then
picking those items for different sales orders during a single travel to the
picking locations. This method is particularly effective for small order picking
or quantities less than case quantities.

details of each item, dimensions, batch lot numbers, other forms are available
to print alongside the BOL.

Description:
In base Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, scrapping defective inventory is
performed using an inventory adjustment journal. Warehouse staff identify items
that are damaged, expired, or otherwise unfit for use. They create an inventory
journal entry, select the relevant items and quantities, and specify a reason
code (such as "scrap" or "defective"). Posting the journal reduces on-hand
inventory and updates financial records, ensuring accurate stock and cost
accounting. The process may include capturing supporting notes, attaching
documentation, and, if configured, triggering workflow approvals for audit
purposes.

Title 5: Scrap expired inventory using journals in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
In base Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps, scrapping expired inventory is
handled through inventory adjustment journals. Warehouse or inventory managers
periodically review stock for expiration, identify expired items, and create an
inventory adjustment journal. They select the expired items, enter the
quantities to be scrapped, and use a reason code such as "expired." Posting the
journal reduces the on-hand inventory and updates financial records accordingly.
This process is straightforward, does not require quality orders, and can be
supported by standard reporting and optional workflow approvals.

Title 5: Scrap expired inventory using journals in Dynamics 365 Business Central
Description:
Post scrap entries through QA journal to reconcile inventory.  This provides a
true measure of inventory consumption and usage, which aids in cost accounting
and inventory yields analysis.

Title 5: Scrap inventory that failed a quality test from a quality order in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
In base Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps, when inventory fails a quality
test, the process typically starts with a quality order. Items are placed in a
quality inspection status, and if they fail, the system can trigger a scrap
action directly from the quality order. This may involve moving the failed items
to a quarantine or scrap location and posting an inventory adjustment to remove
them from available stock. The process can be automated with workflows, and
quality order results are tracked for compliance and reporting.

Title 5: Scrap inventory that failed a quality test from a quality order in Dynamics 365 Business Central
Description:
On Quality Setup, choose option to 'scrap' for failed testing, to account for
lack of consumption

The Manage freight and transportation business process area encompasses the
activities that are done in an organization's transportation management process.
All distribution organizations must be able to track and manage transportation
costs and operations so that they can optimize this critical part of the supply
chain. Meeting this goal requires cross-organization collaboration among
departments such as Logistics, Procurement, Planning, Sales, and Operations.




The exact process for the Manage freight and transportation area varies from
business to business and depends on the industry. However, the basic steps are
the same: The need for transportation is identified. Identification of this need
triggers planning activities, including rating and routing operations. Dock
appointments can then be scheduled for pickup and/or delivery, and necessary
logistics paperwork can be generated. After transportation is completed, freight
invoices can be processed and reconciled against estimates. The definition of
these steps is done as part of the Inventory to deliver end-to-end business
processes and refined in the Define and manage warehouse operations business
process area.



It's essential that you define and establish the business process for Managing
freight and transportation when you first begin to implement Dynamics 365 Supply
Chain Management. This process is a fundamental element for any distribution
company, because it forms the backbone of efficient supply chain operation

Title 6: Maintain search parameters in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Search parameters govern the user experience for full-text customer, prospect, item, product, and product-variant searches. The settings are configured for the legal entity when implementation teams need consistent search behavior during record lookup and manual transaction entry.

The behavior domains include automatically populating customer and item search data, enabling the product-search lookup, deciding whether the product-search dialog is available, limiting the number of returned results, and choosing or remembering the search type. These decisions balance speed, discoverability, and result relevance; they should be aligned with the separately maintained search criteria and indexed business data.

Product, customer, and sales-process owners should agree the intended experience before settings are changed. Search criteria must identify useful source fields, and search data must be current enough for the selected automation and lookup behavior to produce meaningful results.

The parameters affect searches used while identifying customers or prospects and while selecting products or variants on supported sales and purchase lines. Poor settings can hide the lookup, return too many results, or preserve an unsuitable search mode.

Validate common exact and partial searches across representative users and transaction entry scenarios, including result limits and remembered search type. Review all affected search paths after parameter, catalog, naming, or indexed-field changes rather than only confirming that the parameter page saves. Owner mapping requires review before publication.

They are configured when an organization uses the Sales and marketing module and needs consistent behavior across customer-development activities.

Behavior domains include general periods and dates, prospect qualification outcomes, opportunity creation and updates from sales quotations, document handling, campaigns, activities, transaction logging, and number sequences. Sales operations, marketing, and customer-data owners should agree on qualification and quotation policies, default values, logging expectations, and ownership of generated records. The settings affect the creation and maintenance of prospects, customers, opportunities, quotations, campaigns, and activities. Validate them with a representative prospect qualification, quotation status change, campaign, and activity, confirming the intended prompts or automatic record creation.
