Description:
Manages the full lifecycle of active suppliers from onboarding through
relationship termination. Includes maintaining vendor records, updating banking
and contact details, managing electronic ordering channels, monitoring
performance, enforcing compliance, and executing offboarding procedures.

Scope & Outcomes


 * Ensures supplier data remains current and accurate
 * Supports transactional readiness and compliance
 * Enables collaboration and performance tracking
 * Facilitates controlled supplier offboarding
 * Outcomes include enriched vendor profiles, validated banking and tax data,
   active ordering channels, performance insights, and clean termination records



Supplier Management Model
Business Identity
Legal name, registration details, tax IDs, NAICS codes, geography, parent/child
relationships

Contacts & Access
Primary contacts, email, phone, address, role-based access, notification
preferences

Banking & Payment
Bank name, account number, routing code, currency, country, verification status,
payment terms

Demographics & Commercial Markers
Category fit, delivery lanes, capacity, lead times, pricing structures, trade
agreements, contract status

Compliance & Certifications
Insurance, ESG attestations, cybersecurity posture, sanctions/KYC status,
diversity certifications, effective/expiry dates

Performance
Delivery timeliness, quality metrics, responsiveness, dispute rate, claim
history

Ordering Channels
EDI/cXML setup, catalog integration, punchout configuration, approved vendor
list bindings

Lifecycle Status
Active, paused, terminated, reason codes, termination date, reinstatement
eligibility

Data Sources


 * Supplier collaboration portal: profile updates, document uploads,
   certifications
 * ERP: vendor master updates, payment terms, ordering setup
 * Controlled imports: CSV/cXML/API from supplier systems, CLM, performance
   modules
 * Manual entry: vendor group changes, policy flags, offboarding triggers



Operating Model


 * Portal-driven updates: suppliers maintain profiles, submit certifications,
   request changes
 * ERP maintenance: procurement teams manage sensitive fields, enforce workflows
 * Hybrid: portal for routine updates, ERP for critical attributes and
   offboarding



High-Level Process

 1. Maintain Vendor Profile
    Update contact, banking, tax, and demographic data
    Validate certifications and compliance attributes

 2. Manage Ordering Channels
    Configure EDI/cXML, catalogs, punchout setups
    Bind vendors to approved lists and trade agreements

 3. Monitor Performance & Compliance
    Track delivery, quality, responsiveness
    Flag issues, initiate corrective actions

 4. Pause or Restrict Vendor
    Apply status changes, restrict categories, enforce RFQ exclusions

 5. Terminate Relationship
    Record termination reason, date, supporting documents
    Disable ordering channels, notify stakeholders

 6. Review & Refresh
    Schedule periodic reviews of vendor profiles, certifications, performance
    Notify suppliers of expiring documents, request updates

Roles & Responsibilities


 * Procurement manager: owns vendor group assignments, ordering setup,
   offboarding approvals
 * Supplier onboarding operations: validates updates, manages workflows
 * Risk & compliance: maintains KYC/sanctions rules, approves sensitive changes
 * Diversity & inclusion lead: monitors certification validity, reporting
   targets
 * Finance/AP: verifies banking and tax data, ensures auditability
 * Business stakeholders: provide feedback on supplier fit and performance



Dynamics 365 Support


 * Vendor information management: profile updates, banking, tax, compliance
 * Supplier collaboration portal: self-service updates, document uploads
 * Workflow automation: approvals, validations, notifications
 * Purchasing policies: enforce sourcing rules, RFQ eligibility
 * Analytics: dashboards for performance, diversity spend, lifecycle status



Deliverables

 * Updated vendor profiles with validated attributes
 * Active ordering channels and approved vendor lists
 * Performance dashboards and compliance reports
 * Offboarding records with audit trail
 * Diversity spend and lifecycle status metrics

Description:
Evaluates supplier performance across strategic and operational dimensions using
defined KPIs, stakeholder feedback, and transactional data. Covers quality,
delivery, pricing, compliance, and service metrics. Supports continuous
improvement, risk mitigation, and sourcing decisions.

Scope & Outcomes
Monitors supplier effectiveness post-onboarding through structured reviews and
analytics. Identifies trends, anomalies, and non-conformances. Outcomes include
performance dashboards, supplier scorecards, risk flags, and improvement plans.

Performance Evaluation Model

 * Delivery Metrics
   
   * % In Full, On Time (IFOT)
   * Delivery lead time variance
   * Missed delivery windows
 * Quality Metrics
   
   * Failed quality inspections
   * Non-conformance reports
   * Warranty claims / service issues
 * Pricing & Commercial Trends
   
   * Price variance analysis
   * Unexpected cost increases
   * Contract compliance
 * Forecast vs Actuals
   
   * Order forecast accuracy
   * Volume adherence
 * Stakeholder Feedback
   
   * Internal surveys (procurement, operations)
   * External surveys (supplier self-assessment)
 * Risk & Compliance
   
   * Recall incidents
   * Sanctions / KYC status changes
   * Insurance / ESG / cybersecurity posture
 * Service & Support
   
   * Responsiveness
   * Dispute resolution rate
   * Claim history

Data Sources

 * ERP receiving and quality modules
 * Supplier collaboration portal (self-assessments, service logs)
 * CLM systems (contract compliance)
 * Manual entry (non-conformance reports, survey results)
 * Controlled imports (CSV, cXML, API from performance systems)

Operating Model

 * Portal-driven performance updates and surveys
 * ERP-based transactional data capture
 * Hybrid model for manual and automated inputs

High-Level Process

 1. Define KPIs & Thresholds
    
    * Set performance metrics by category, region, business unit
 2. Configure Data Capture
    
    * Enable ERP modules, portal forms, survey templates
 3. Collect Performance Data
    
    * Intake from transactions, surveys, supplier inputs
 4. Analyze & Score
    
    * Compute KPIs, identify anomalies, flag risks
 5. Review & Validate
    
    * Procurement reviews scorecards, confirms issues
 6. Publish Dashboards
    
    * Share performance insights with sourcing teams
 7. Trigger Actions
    
    * Initiate improvement plans, pause sourcing, escalate issues
 8. Monitor & Refresh
    
    * Schedule reviews, notify suppliers, update metrics

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Procurement manager: owns KPI definitions, reviews performance, triggers
   actions
 * Supplier onboarding / operations: manages portal inputs, validates data
 * Risk / compliance: monitors sanctions, KYC, ESG, cybersecurity
 * Diversity & inclusion: tracks diversity performance metrics
 * Finance / AP: validates pricing, payment terms, cost anomalies
 * Business stakeholders: provide feedback on supplier fit and service

Dynamics 365 Support

 * Vendor information management: stores performance attributes
 * Supplier collaboration portal: collects surveys, service logs
 * Workflow automation: routes reviews, flags issues
 * Purchasing policies: enforce sourcing restrictions based on performance
 * Analytics (Power BI / Microsoft Fabric): visualize KPIs, trends, risk
   indicators

Deliverables

 * Supplier scorecards
 * Performance dashboards
 * Non-conformance logs
 * Survey results
 * Recall reports
 * Improvement plans
 * Risk flags and escalation records

Title 6: Create and configure financial period close workspace in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
The Financial period close workspace provides a coordinated view of closing tasks, due dates, dependencies, owners, and completion status across companies and accounting areas. It is used when an organization needs a repeatable close process with clear accountability and visibility into overdue, blocked, and remaining work.

Before using the workspace, configure resources, task areas, working-day calendars, close templates, and closing schedules. Decide which tasks apply to each company, who owns them, their relative due dates and times, task links, and dependencies. Different templates can support month-end, quarter-end, or year-end processes, but each closing schedule uses one template.

The configured schedule generates the tasks monitored in the workspace and retains completion history for reporting and audit analysis. Validate a representative schedule by confirming task generation, company assignments, due dates, dependency blocking, links, and user visibility. Review templates and calendars when responsibilities, legal entities, close procedures, or holidays change; closing a schedule removes it from the active workspace and prevents further task edits.

Title 5: Review warranty claims/servicing for suppliers in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description: Review warranty claims/servicing for suppliers

Evaluates supplier performance across strategic and operational dimensions using
defined KPIs, stakeholder feedback, and transactional data. Covers quality,
delivery, pricing, compliance, and service metrics. Supports continuous
improvement, risk mitigation, and sourcing decisions.

Scope & Outcomes
Monitors supplier effectiveness post-onboarding through structured reviews and
analytics. Identifies trends, anomalies, and non-conformances. Outcomes include
performance dashboards, supplier scorecards, risk flags, and improvement plans.

Performance Evaluation Model

 * Delivery Metrics
   
   * % In Full, On Time (IFOT)
   * Delivery lead time variance
   * Missed delivery windows
 * Quality Metrics
   
   * Failed quality inspections
   * Non-conformance reports
   * Warranty claims / service issues
 * Pricing & Commercial Trends
   
   * Price variance analysis
   * Unexpected cost increases
   * Contract compliance
 * Forecast vs Actuals
   
   * Order forecast accuracy
   * Volume adherence
 * Stakeholder Feedback
   
   * Internal surveys (procurement, operations)
   * External surveys (supplier self-assessment)
 * Risk & Compliance
   
   * Recall incidents
   * Sanctions / KYC status changes
   * Insurance / ESG / cybersecurity posture
 * Service & Support
   
   * Responsiveness
   * Dispute resolution rate
   * Claim history

Data Sources

 * ERP receiving and quality modules
 * Supplier collaboration portal (self-assessments, service logs)
 * CLM systems (contract compliance)
 * Manual entry (non-conformance reports, survey results)
 * Controlled imports (CSV, cXML, API from performance systems)

Operating Model

 * Portal-driven performance updates and surveys
 * ERP-based transactional data capture
 * Hybrid model for manual and automated inputs

High-Level Process

 1. Define KPIs & Thresholds
    
    * Set performance metrics by category, region, business unit
 2. Configure Data Capture
    
    * Enable ERP modules, portal forms, survey templates
 3. Collect Performance Data
    
    * Intake from transactions, surveys, supplier inputs
 4. Analyze & Score
    
    * Compute KPIs, identify anomalies, flag risks
 5. Review & Validate
    
    * Procurement reviews scorecards, confirms issues
 6. Publish Dashboards
    
    * Share performance insights with sourcing teams
 7. Trigger Actions
    
    * Initiate improvement plans, pause sourcing, escalate issues
 8. Monitor & Refresh
    
    * Schedule reviews, notify suppliers, update metrics

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Procurement manager: owns KPI definitions, reviews performance, triggers
   actions
 * Supplier onboarding / operations: manages portal inputs, validates data
 * Risk / compliance: monitors sanctions, KYC, ESG, cybersecurity
 * Diversity & inclusion: tracks diversity performance metrics
 * Finance / AP: validates pricing, payment terms, cost anomalies
 * Business stakeholders: provide feedback on supplier fit and service

Dynamics 365 Support

 * Vendor information management: stores performance attributes
 * Supplier collaboration portal: collects surveys, service logs
 * Workflow automation: routes reviews, flags issues
 * Purchasing policies: enforce sourcing restrictions based on performance
 * Analytics (Power BI / Microsoft Fabric): visualize KPIs, trends, risk
   indicators

Deliverables

 * Supplier scorecards
 * Performance dashboards
 * Non-conformance logs
 * Survey results
 * Recall reports
 * Improvement plans
 * Risk flags and escalation records

Description:
Manage Supplier Risk involves identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks
across the supplier lifecycle. It includes evaluating suppliers during
onboarding, monitoring ongoing risk factors, and enforcing compliance. The
process is supported by both internal governance frameworks and Dynamics 365 SCM
features.


SCOPE & OUTCOMES

 * Scope: Covers operational, financial, regulatory, privacy, societal, and
   geopolitical risks.
 * Outcomes:
   * Risk-tiered supplier profiles
   * Alerts for high-risk vendors
   * Risk dashboards and reports
   * Compliance enforcement and audit trails
   * Informed sourcing decisions


RISK MANAGEMENT MODEL

Risk Dimensions

 * Operational: Contract types, subcontractor usage, evergreen agreements
 * Regulatory: Country corruption index, human rights, health & safety standards
 * Privacy: Data processing roles, volume, classification, security posture
 * Societal: Accessibility, sustainability, environmental impact
 * Financial: Supplier financial health, currency volatility, credit ratings
 * Security: Infosec posture, cybersecurity attestations, SCSAC assessments

Risk Assessment Tools

 * Supplier Risk Model: Calculates inherent and residual risk using internal and
   external data
 * Supply Risk Assessment Workspace (D365 SCM):
   
   * Embedded Power BI reports
   * On-time in-full (OTIF) ratings
   * Risk scoring based on planned purchase orders
   * Forecasting future supply risk based on historical performance

Governance & Enforcement

 * Supplier Accountability Office (SAO): Manages violations, audits, and due
   diligence
 * SGME (Supplier Governance, Monitoring and Enforcement): Tracks financial
   health, conflicts of interest, anti-corruption, and societal impact
 * SCSAC (Supply Chain Security Assessment & Consulting): Provides security risk
   profiling and recommendations for third-party suppliers


DATA SOURCES

 * ERP & SCM: Supplier master data, transactional history, planned orders
 * Supplier Portal: Self-assessments, certifications, profile updates
 * Power BI: Embedded dashboards for risk visualization
 * External Registries: Financial ratings, ESG scores, sanctions lists


OPERATING MODEL

 * Portal-driven: Suppliers submit risk-related data and certifications
 * Automated Imports: Risk data from external sources and registries
 * Manual Oversight: Procurement and compliance teams validate and monitor


HIGH-LEVEL PROCESS

 1. Define Risk Criteria: Set thresholds for each risk dimension
 2. Configure Risk Model: Enable scoring logic and data sources
 3. Collect Risk Data: Intake from portal, ERP, external feeds
 4. Assess & Score: Compute risk tiers and flags
 5. Review & Validate: Procurement and compliance teams review flagged suppliers
 6. Publish Dashboards: Share risk insights with sourcing teams
 7. Trigger Actions: Escalate, restrict, or offboard high-risk suppliers
 8. Monitor & Refresh: Schedule reviews and update risk profiles


ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Procurement: Owns risk thresholds, reviews flagged suppliers
 * Compliance: Maintains KYC, sanctions, ESG rules
 * Supplier Onboarding: Validates submissions and manages workflows
 * Security Teams: Conduct SCSAC assessments and provide recommendations
 * Finance: Verifies financial health and auditability


DYNAMICS 365 SUPPORT

 * SCM Risk Workspace: Central hub for supplier risk metrics and reports [3]
   [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/supply-chain/procurement/supply-risk-assessment-overview]
 * Supplier Risk Model: Built-in scoring engine for risk classification [2]
   [https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/MyProcureWeb/SitePages/Supplier-Accountability-Office.aspx?web=1]
 * Supplier Portal: Self-service updates and certifications [7]
   [https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/BusinessApplicationsContentHub/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7b477473DA-014D-40C7-AE92-480CFF34EC3A%7d&file=Dynamics%20365%20PAB%20SCM%20%26%20Commerce%20Focus%20Group.pptx&action=edit&mobileredirect=true&DefaultItemOpen=1]
 * Power BI Integration: Visualize risk trends and supplier performance

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


DELIVERABLES

 * Risk taxonomy and scoring framework
 * Configured supplier risk model and dashboards
 * Supplier risk profiles and audit logs
 * Alerts and escalation workflows
 * SCSAC and SGME compliance reports

Deliverables

Description:
This process governs the setup, maintenance, and optimization of supplier
pricing across the lifecycle—from onboarding through active engagement. It
includes default pricing, manual and automated updates, integration with
external systems, discounting mechanisms, vendor-specific pricing via trade
agreements, vendor group pricing, and rebate programs.


SCOPE & OUTCOMES

Scope

 * Default and negotiated pricing
 * Manual and automated price updates
 * Integration with pricing APIs and external systems
 * Vendor-specific and group-based pricing
 * Rebate and incentive programs

Outcomes

 * Accurate, current pricing across vendors and categories
 * Enforced pricing policies and trade agreements
 * Visibility into discounts, rebates, and pricing trends
 * Optimized procurement spend and compliance


PRICING MANAGEMENT MODEL

Default Pricing

 * Base price setup per item or service
 * Used when no trade agreement or discount applies

Manual & Automated Updates

 * Manual entry via ERP or supplier portal
 * Automated updates via APIs or integrations
 * Effective date ranges, currency, and unit price tracking

Trade Agreements

 * Vendor-specific pricing rules
 * Quantity-based discounts, tiered pricing
 * Binding agreements linked to approved vendor lists 

Vendor Groups

 * Shared pricing across vendor classifications
 * Category-level pricing enforcement

Rebate Programs

 * Structured rebate agreements configured in Dynamics 365
 * Eligibility criteria, approval workflows
 * Performance-based incentives and retrospective discounts

Discounting & Promotions

 * Negotiated discounts applied to unit price
 * Tracked via authenticated APIs and SCM workflows


DATA SOURCES

 * ERP: Vendor master data, trade agreements, pricing records
 * Supplier Portal: Self-service updates, rebate submissions
 * Pricing APIs: Real-time price retrieval, discount validation 
 * CLM Systems: Contract-linked pricing terms
 * Rebate Modules: Incentive tracking and analysis 


OPERATING MODEL

 * Portal-driven: Suppliers maintain pricing profiles, submit rebate claims
 * ERP-integrated: Procurement teams manage trade agreements, pricing rules
 * Hybrid: Combines manual oversight with automated updates and validations


HIGH-LEVEL PROCESS

 1. Define Pricing Strategy
    
    * Set default prices, discount tiers, rebate eligibility

 2. Configure Pricing Records
    
    * Create trade agreements, vendor group pricing

 3. Enable Supplier Portal
    
    * Publish pricing templates, rebate forms

 4. Collect & Validate Pricing Data
    
    * Intake from portal, APIs, manual entry

 5. Apply Pricing Rules
    
    * Enforce trade agreements, discount thresholds

 6. Monitor & Adjust
    
    * Track price variance, rebate performance

 7. Audit & Report
    
    * Generate spend analytics, rebate dashboards


ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Procurement: Owns pricing strategy, trade agreements
 * Finance/AP: Validates pricing, rebates, audit trails
 * Supplier Onboarding: Ensures pricing setup during onboarding
 * Business Stakeholders: Provide input on pricing fit and performance


DYNAMICS 365 SUPPORT

 * Vendor Information Management: Pricing fields, trade agreements
 * Supplier Collaboration Portal: Price updates, rebate submissions
 * SCM: Purchase agreement workflows, pricing enforcement
 * Analytics: Power BI dashboards for pricing trends, rebate performance


DELIVERABLES

 * Configured pricing records and trade agreements
 * Rebate program setup and approval workflows
 * Pricing dashboards and spend analytics
 * Audit logs and compliance reports

 * Controlled procurement spend
 * Digitally managed contracts with searchable metadata
 * Strategic and transactional supplier relationships

   compliance tagging
 * Dynamics 365 SCM: Manages purchase agreements, trade terms, and supplier

   and profile maintenance

   performance


ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Procurement Managers: Own sourcing strategy, issue requests, evaluate bids,
   and approve contracts
 * Legal & Compliance: Review contract terms, ensure regulatory alignment
 * Finance/AP: Monitor spend, validate pricing, enforce budget controls
 * Business Stakeholders: Define requirements, participate in evaluations, and

Description:
Evaluates supplier responses to RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs using structured and
unstructured methods. This process supports fair, transparent, and data-driven
selection of vendors based on technical, commercial, and strategic criteria. It
includes use of questionnaires, scorecards, site visits, and review of one-time
vendors, write-in products, and unsolicited proposals.

Scope & Outcomes

 * Applies evaluation frameworks to supplier bids
 * Supports scoring, validation, and stakeholder review
 * Outcomes include supplier rankings, bid scorecards, sourcing decisions, and
   documentation of rationale

Bid Evaluation Model

 * Structured Inputs
   
   * Questionnaires and forms submitted via supplier portal
   * Standardized templates for technical, commercial, and compliance criteria
   * Scorecards with weighted metrics and scoring rubrics

 * Unstructured Inputs
   
   * Site visit reports
   * Stakeholder feedback
   * Write-in products on purchase requisitions
   * Product suggestions and unsolicited proposals

 * Vendor Types
   
   * Approved vendors
   * One-time vendors (used for niche or urgent needs)
   * Prospective vendors from RFIs or unsolicited proposals

 * Evaluation Criteria
   
   * Price competitiveness
   * Technical fit
   * Delivery capability
   * Compliance and certifications
   * Diversity and sustainability attributes
   * Risk profile and performance history

Operating Model

 * Portal-driven: Suppliers submit bids, questionnaires, and documents
 * Manual review: Procurement and stakeholders assess site visits, write-ins,
   and proposals
 * Hybrid: Combines automated scoring with human judgment and qualitative review

High-Level Process

 1. Define Evaluation Framework
    Set scoring criteria, weightings, and stakeholder roles

 2. Collect Bid Responses
    Intake via supplier portal, email, or manual entry

 3. Score Structured Inputs
    Apply scorecards to questionnaires and pricing sheets

 4. Review Unstructured Inputs
    Assess site visit findings, write-in products, and proposals

 5. Rank Suppliers
    Aggregate scores and feedback to generate rankings

 6. Validate and Approve
    Review by category managers and sourcing leads

 7. Document Rationale
    Record evaluation outcomes, scoring rationale, and sourcing decisions

 8. Publish Results
    Share selected suppliers with sourcing and contract teams

Dynamics 365 Support

 * Supplier collaboration portal: Bid submission, questionnaires, document
   uploads
 * Vendor information management: Stores evaluation results, scorecards, and
   rationale
 * Workflow automation: Routes evaluations, approvals, and notifications
 * Purchasing policies: Enforce sourcing rules and vendor eligibility
 * Analytics (Power BI): Visualize bid comparisons, scoring trends, and sourcing
   outcomes

Deliverables

 * Evaluation templates and scorecards
 * Site visit reports and stakeholder feedback forms
 * Bid comparison dashboards
 * Approved vendor list with rationale
 * Documentation of sourcing decisions and audit trail

Manages procurement spend across categories, business units, and suppliers.
Includes monitoring budget adherence, handling overages, enforcing signing
limits, and triggering workflow escalations. Supports proactive spend
governance, policy enforcement, and financial accountability.


SCOPE & OUTCOMES

 * Tracks actual vs. forecasted spend
 * Flags budget overages and policy violations
 * Enforces signing limits and approval hierarchies
 * Escalates spend exceptions via workflows
 * Provides visibility into spend by category, supplier, region, and cost center

Outcomes include:

 * Controlled procurement spend
 * Reduced maverick buying
 * Improved budget compliance
 * Spend dashboards and audit trails


SPEND MANAGEMENT MODEL

Spend Dimensions

 * Category: goods/services classification
 * Supplier: strategic vs. tail vendors
 * Region: geography-based spend tracking
 * Business Unit / Cost Center: internal allocation
 * Purchase Type: PO, non-PO, contract-based

Controls

 * Budget thresholds
 * Signing limits by role
 * Escalation workflows
 * Policy flags (e.g., preferred vendor enforcement)

Exceptions

 * Budget overages
 * Unauthorized purchases
 * Non-compliant suppliers
 * Emergency buys


OPERATING MODEL

 * Portal-driven: Requisitioners submit purchase requests via supplier portal or
   ERP
 * Automated workflows: Escalate based on spend thresholds, signing limits, or
   policy violations
 * Manual oversight: Finance and procurement review flagged transactions


HIGH-LEVEL PROCESS

 1. Define Spend Policies
    
    * Set signing limits, budget thresholds, preferred vendor rules

 2. Configure Spend Controls
    
    * Enable approval workflows, policy flags, budget checks

 3. Monitor Spend Activity
    
    * Track actual vs. forecasted spend across dimensions

 4. Flag Exceptions
    
    * Identify overages, unauthorized purchases, non-compliant vendors

 5. Escalate for Review
    
    * Route flagged transactions to approvers based on rules

 6. Approve or Reject
    
    * Approvers validate, reject, or reassign based on policy

 7. Report & Analyze
    
    * Generate dashboards for spend trends, violations, savings

 8. Audit & Improve
    
    * Review spend patterns, refine thresholds, update policies


ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Procurement: Owns spend policies, reviews exceptions
 * Finance/AP: Validates budget adherence, signing limits
 * Business Stakeholders: Provide input on spend needs, exceptions
 * Category Managers: Monitor category-level spend, enforce sourcing rules


DYNAMICS 365 SUPPORT

 * Vendor Information Management: Links spend to supplier profiles
 * Purchasing Policies: Enforce spend controls, preferred vendor usage
 * Workflow Automation: Escalation routing, approvals
 * Analytics (Power BI): Spend dashboards, exception tracking
 * Budget Integration: Forecast vs. actual spend comparison


DELIVERABLES

 * Spend policy matrix
 * Configured approval workflows
 * Exception handling rules
 * Spend dashboards by category, supplier, region
 * Audit logs of approvals, escalations, violations

Description:
This process governs the operational execution of purchasing goods and services,
including creation and management of purchase requisitions, purchase orders,
blanket orders, planned purchases, and returns. It ensures that procurement
activities align with approved budgets, sourcing strategies, and supplier
contracts. The process supports consolidation of requisitions, automated PO
generation, and integration with financial and inventory systems.

Scope & Outcomes

 * Initiates procurement through requisitions and planned purchases
 * Converts approved requisitions into purchase orders or blanket orders
 * Manages vendor-specific pricing, delivery terms, and order confirmations
 * Supports returns and adjustments for non-conforming goods
 * Consolidates requisitions across departments or cost centers
 * Ensures compliance with budget limits and approval workflows
 * Outcomes include accurate PO records, timely deliveries, validated returns,
   and optimized procurement cycles

Key Components

 * Purchase Requisitions: Internal requests for goods/services, routed through
   approval workflows. Can be consolidated across business units or cost
   centers.
 * Purchase Orders (POs): Formal orders issued to suppliers, generated manually
   or automatically from approved requisitions or planned purchases.
 * Blanket Orders: Long-term agreements with suppliers for recurring purchases,
   supporting release schedules and quantity tracking.
 * Planned Purchases: Forecast-driven procurement based on demand planning,
   linked to production or project schedules.
 * Returns: Managed through return orders or credit memos for defective, excess,
   or incorrect goods.
 * Requisition Consolidation: Combines multiple requests into a single PO to
   optimize supplier engagement and reduce administrative overhead.

Technology Support

 * Dynamics 365 SCM
   
   * Purchase requisition and PO workflows
   * Blanket order management
   * Planned purchase integration with MRP and demand forecasting
   * Return order processing and inventory adjustments
   * Budget control and approval routing
 * Dynamics 365 Business Central
   
   * Simplified PO creation and vendor management
   * Purchase invoice matching and payment processing
   * Return handling and credit memo generation
   * Integration with financial dimensions and cost centers

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Requesters: Initiate requisitions, provide specifications, confirm receipt
 * Procurement Managers: Review requisitions, issue POs, manage supplier

Formalizes procurement commitments by issuing purchase orders (POs) to
suppliers. POs are generated from approved purchase requisitions, purchase
agreements, RFQs, or directly for project-based, intercompany, or drop shipment
scenarios. Supports integration with external systems such as Field Service or
Asset Management for spare parts and service-linked purchases.

Scope & Outcomes
Covers creation, validation, and transmission of POs across various procurement
scenarios.
Outcomes include:

 * Accurate PO records linked to sourcing documents
 * Supplier commitment to pricing, delivery, and terms
 * Visibility into procurement obligations across business units and systems
 * Support for direct delivery, intercompany trade, and service-linked purchases

PO Creation Scenarios

 * From Purchase Requisition: Converts approved requisitions into POs with
   validated budget and sourcing details
 * From Purchase Agreement: Uses pre-negotiated pricing and terms for recurring
   purchases
 * From RFQ: Selects winning bid and generates PO with agreed terms
 * Project-Based Purchases: Links PO to project ID, task, or milestone for cost
   tracking
 * Intercompany Trade: Issues PO to internal legal entity with mirrored sales
   order
 * Drop Shipment / Direct Delivery: PO sent to supplier for delivery directly to
   customer or field location
 * Spare Parts / Maintenance: POs triggered by Field Service or Asset Management
   systems for parts replenishment or service execution

Key Attributes Captured

 * Supplier ID, legal entity, delivery address
 * Item or category, quantity, unit price, currency
 * Delivery date, payment terms, tax group
 * Project ID, cost center, business unit
 * PO type (standard, blanket, intercompany, drop ship)
 * Linked documents (requisition, agreement, RFQ)

Operating Model

 * Portal-driven: Procurement teams or requesters initiate PO creation via
   workspace
 * Automated: System-generated POs from requisitions, agreements, or external
   triggers
 * Integrated: APIs and connectors link PO creation to Field Service, Asset
   Management, or external planning systems
 * Workflow-enabled: Approval routing based on spend thresholds, category, or
   business unit

Technology Support

 * Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: PO creation, approval workflows,
   intercompany trade, drop shipment, and project linkage
 * Dynamics 365 Business Central: Simplified PO issuance, invoice matching, and
   vendor management
 * Field Service / Asset Management: Triggers PO creation for parts and services
 * Workflow Automation: Approval routing, notifications, and audit trails
 * Power BI: PO analytics, spend tracking, supplier performance

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Requesters: Confirm PO details, receive goods/services
 * Procurement Managers: Create, review, and approve POs
 * Finance / AP: Validate pricing, match invoices, ensure auditability
 * Category Managers: Oversee PO compliance with sourcing strategy
 * Project Managers / Field Technicians: Initiate service-linked POs, confirm
   delivery

Deliverables

 * Issued purchase orders with linked sourcing documents
 * PO status dashboards (open, confirmed, received, invoiced)
 * Audit logs of approvals and changes
 * Spend reports by category, supplier, and project

Title 5: Create purchase order from request for quotations in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Create purchase order from request for quotations in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain
Management



Organizations issue RFQs when they want to receive competitive offers from
several vendors for the items or services that they must purchase.You can create
an RFQ case from planned orders, from a purchase requisition, or by manual
entry. The RFQ case is the base document that you use to issue an RFQ to each
vendor. 


In an RFQ, you ask vendors to provide the prices and delivery times for the item
quantities that you specify. You can also ask vendors to specify whether there
are any incidental charges, such as shipping costs, or any discounts for large
orders or early payment of the vendor invoice.



The RFQ process consists of the following tasks:

 * Create and send an RFQ to one or more vendors.
 * Receive and register bids (RFQ replies).
 * Transfer bids that you accept to a purchase order, purchase agreement, or
   purchase requisition.

Manages post-issuance lifecycle of purchase orders (POs), including updates,
cancellations, delivery adjustments, and follow-ups. Supports change management
workflows for quantity, pricing, delivery dates, and cross-docking. Ensures
procurement agility, supplier coordination, and compliance with approval
policies.

Scope & Outcomes
Covers all modifications to open POs across procurement scenarios.
Outcomes include:

 * Accurate, up-to-date PO records
 * Controlled change approvals
 * Timely supplier communication
 * Visibility into PO status and fulfillment

Change Management Scenarios

 * Quantity Adjustments: Increase or decrease ordered quantities based on demand
   or supplier constraints
 * Pricing Updates: Reflect negotiated changes, discounts, or corrections
 * Delivery Information: Modify delivery dates, locations, or methods (e.g.,
   cross-docking)
 * Partial or Full Cancellation: Cancel entire PO or specific lines due to
   budget changes, supplier issues, or sourcing shifts
 * Follow-ups: Track PO status, confirm delivery, escalate delays

Supported PO Types

 * Standard POs
 * Intercompany POs
 * Drop shipment / direct delivery
 * Project-based POs
 * Blanket order releases

Operating Model

 * Portal-driven: Procurement teams and requesters initiate changes via
   workspace
 * Workflow-enabled: Approval routing for sensitive changes (e.g., pricing,
   quantity)
 * System-integrated: Updates reflected across linked systems (inventory,
   finance, project management)
 * Supplier collaboration: Notifications and confirmations for PO changes

Technology Support

 * Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
   
   * PO change tracking
   * Delivery schedule updates
   * Cross-docking configuration
   * Workflow approvals
 * Dynamics 365 Business Central
   
   * PO editing
   * Cancellation handling
   * Invoice matching
 * Field Service / Asset Management
   
   * PO updates for service-linked parts and maintenance
 * Workflow Automation
   
   * Escalation routing, notifications, audit trails

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Procurement Managers: Initiate and approve PO changes, coordinate with
   suppliers
 * Requesters: Request updates, confirm delivery
 * Finance / AP: Validate pricing changes, ensure auditability
 * Warehouse / Receiving: Confirm delivery, initiate returns or adjustments
 * Project Managers / Field Technicians: Trigger updates for project or
   service-linked POs

Deliverables

 * Updated PO records with change history
 * Cancellation logs and audit trails
 * Delivery schedule reports
 * Supplier communication records
 * PO performance dashboard

Description:
Establishes long-term purchasing arrangements with suppliers for recurring goods
or services. Blanket orders define pricing, quantities, and delivery schedules
over a specified period, streamlining procurement and reducing administrative
overhead. In F&O, these are managed as purchase agreements and can be linked to
requisitions, purchase orders, and trade agreements.

Scope & Outcomes
Supports strategic sourcing by locking in terms with preferred suppliers.
Enables automated PO creation against agreed terms, improves spend forecasting,
and enforces compliance with negotiated pricing and delivery conditions.
Outcomes include:

 * Validated purchase agreements with supplier commitments
 * Automated PO generation based on releases
 * Spend tracking against agreement thresholds
 * Reduced manual entry and improved procurement efficiency

Types of Purchase Agreements

 * Value Commitment: Specifies a total monetary value to be purchased over time.
 * Quantity Commitment: Defines specific quantities of items to be procured.
 * Product Category Commitment: Applies to a category of items rather than
   specific SKUs.
 * Blanket Orders with Release Schedules: Used for recurring deliveries with
   predefined intervals or triggers.

Operating Model
Procurement teams create purchase agreements in F&O, linking them to vendor
records and trade agreements. Agreements can be referenced in requisitions and
POs, enabling automated enforcement of pricing and terms. Release orders are
generated manually or automatically based on demand, forecasts, or consumption.

Technology Support

 * Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations: Manages purchase agreements, release
   orders, and trade agreement enforcement.
 * Supplier Collaboration Portal: Enables suppliers to view agreement terms,
   confirm releases, and submit updates.
 * Workflow Automation: Routes agreements for approval, monitors thresholds, and
   triggers alerts.
 * Power BI: Provides dashboards for agreement utilization, supplier
   performance, and spend tracking.

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Procurement Managers: Define agreement terms, negotiate with suppliers, and
   monitor usage.
 * Finance/AP: Validate pricing, ensure auditability, and manage payment terms.
 * Category Managers: Oversee category-level agreements and supplier compliance.
 * Requesters: Reference agreements in requisitions and confirm deliveries.

Deliverables

 * Executed purchase agreements with supplier terms
 * Release order records linked to agreements
 * Spend utilization reports and compliance dashboards
 * Audit logs of agreement changes and approvals

Title 5: Create a purchase order return in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description:
Create a Purchase order return



A purchase return order is created by using the Credit note action to copy lines
from a vendor invoice document to a new purchase order ("referenced return").
Alternatively, a Return Purchase Order can also be created manually without
references (ties) back to a previous invoice ("non referenced return).


A Return Purchase Order is a unique purchase order "type" and follows a
different set of requirements than a standard purchase order. A return purchase
order must be confirmed (same as a standard purchase order) before
transactions can be performed (such as the shipment of the goods back to the
vendor).

Description:
Combines multiple purchase requisitions into a single consolidated requisition
or purchase order to streamline procurement, reduce administrative overhead, and
optimize supplier engagement. This process is especially useful when multiple
departments or cost centers request similar items or services within a close
timeframe.

Scope & Outcomes
Supports consolidation of requisitions based on item, category, supplier,
delivery date, or business unit.
Outcomes include:

 * Fewer purchase orders issued
 * Improved negotiation leverage with suppliers
 * Reduced processing time and manual effort
 * Better alignment with blanket orders and purchase agreements

Consolidation Scenarios

 * Multiple requisitions for the same item from different requesters or
   departments
 * Category-based requisitions for indirect spend (e.g., office supplies, IT
   equipment)
 * Requisitions linked to planned purchases or forecasted demand
 * Consolidation across projects or cost centers for shared services or assets

Operating Model
Procurement teams use the Demand Consolidation workspace in F&O to identify and
merge requisitions based on predefined rules.
System suggests consolidation opportunities based on item match, supplier,
delivery window, and budget availability.
Approved consolidated requisitions are converted into purchase orders or linked
to existing purchase agreements.

Technology Support

 * Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations
   
   * Demand Consolidation workspace
   * Purchase requisition management
   * Budget control and approval workflows
   * Integration with purchase agreements and trade agreements
 * Workflow automation for approvals and notifications
 * Power BI dashboards for tracking consolidation efficiency and spend impact

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Requesters: Submit requisitions with accurate item/category details
 * Procurement Managers: Review consolidation suggestions, approve merged
   requisitions, issue POs
 * Finance/AP: Validate budget availability and audit compliance
 * Category Managers: Oversee consolidation rules and supplier alignment

Deliverables

 * Consolidated requisition records
 * Linked purchase orders
 * Spend optimization reports
 * Audit logs of consolidation actions and approvals

Description:
Analyzes supply and purchase plans to ensure timely procurement aligned with
demand forecasts, inventory levels, and project needs. This process supports
master planning activities by reviewing planned purchase orders, delayed or
short receipts, and responding to action messages. It enables proactive
decision-making to adjust supply plans, confirm procurement actions, and
maintain operational continuity.

Scope & Outcomes
Covers review and adjustment of planned purchase orders, confirmation of supply
actions, and resolution of supply exceptions.
Outcomes include:

 * Validated planned purchase orders
 * Adjusted supply schedules based on delays or shortages
 * Executed action messages (e.g., expedite, postpone, cancel)
 * Improved supply chain responsiveness and procurement accuracy

Planning Scenarios

 * Planned Purchase Orders: Generated from demand forecasts, MRP, or project
   schedules; reviewed for confirmation or adjustment.
 * Delayed Receipts: Identifies overdue deliveries; triggers follow-up or
   rescheduling.
 * Short Receipts: Flags partial deliveries; initiates corrective actions or
   supplier communication.
 * Action Messages: System-generated recommendations to expedite, delay, cancel,
   or change orders based on updated planning data.
 * Project-Based Supply: Ensures alignment of supply plans with project
   timelines and resource needs.

Operating Model

 * Procurement and planning teams review supply plans in master planning
   workspace.
 * Action messages are processed to adjust procurement actions.
 * Planned orders are confirmed or modified based on supply chain constraints
   and business priorities.
 * Integration with inventory, production, and project modules ensures holistic
   planning.

Technology Support

 * Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
   
   * Master planning engine for generating planned orders
   * Action message processing for supply adjustments
   * Integration with inventory, production, and project modules
 * Business Central
   
   * Simplified planning and purchase order generation
   * Visibility into supply schedules and procurement actions
 * Power BI
   
   * Dashboards for supply plan performance, delayed receipts, and action
     message execution

Roles & Responsibilities

 * Procurement Managers: Confirm planned orders, execute action messages,
   coordinate with suppliers.
 * Planners: Analyze supply plans, adjust schedules, validate demand forecasts.
 * Warehouse / Receiving: Report short or delayed receipts, support corrective
   actions.
 * Project Managers: Align supply plans with project milestones and resource
   needs.

be in place before the vendor invoice process.

measure how well a vendor helps a company achieve its business goals:.

> ordered
> Defect rates: The rate at which a vendor delivers defective items

Description:
The project to profit process can be used in any project-oriented business. The
process starts when a deal is won and ends when you invoice the customer for the
services you have provided. The project to profit business process can be
adapted to fit the specific needs and requirements of any organization which
carries out some of its work by dividing it into various projects. Industries
where this is common include consulting, professional services,
engineer-to-order manufacturing, construction, entertainment, and many others.




For example, in consulting services, a project typically includes business
analysis, to identify areas where the client business can improve customer
experience, streamline operations, increase revenue by expanding services or
entering new markets, or meet other client goals.



Next, the consultant designs a solution based on the customer�s requirements
gathered during business analysis. Realizing the design might include expanding
service offerings, redesigning a business process, defining a strategy for
entering new markets, implementing a supporting technology or system, and so on.
And prior to profitably executing such a project, a consulting firm needs to
identify appropriate opportunities in its market and close corresponding sales
of the project services it will deliver.



Dynamics 365 includes tools to help project-oriented organizations manage leads,
opportunities, the quoting and contracting process, and detailed planning for
projects. By using work breakdown structures, organizations can easily define
the scope and tasks that need to be completed for a given project. These tools
are tightly integrated in Dynamics 365 Project Operations with Project for the
Web and our Unified Resource Scheduling.



Once project initiation is complete the next step is to run the project and bill
for it as agreed in a governing contract. During project execution, Dynamics 365
includes a variety of tools to help organizations schedule resources, track
costs, time, and materials that are used to deliver the service, bill and
collect revenue and record corresponding accounting entries. Dynamics 365 also
includes tools to help organizations monitor client feedback and adjust the
service offering as needed. Similarly, Dynamics 365 includes several tools that
can be used throughout the project lifecycle to optimize profitability by
measuring key performance indicators, such as revenue growth, actuals versus
estimated budgets, customer satisfaction, and employee productivity. Project
managers can use this data to make adjustments and improve the service offering
to ensure the project continues to generate profit and meets business goals.



In summary, project-oriented businesses can use the project to profit process to
sell, analyze, design, implement, and monitor solutions that enable them to
increase profitability, streamline operations, and provide better service to
their clients. The process can be tailored to fit the specific needs and goals
of the organization, regardless of whether it involves technology or not.

capabilities of the business itself, rather than to bill a third party and the
outcome of the project may be the creation of a capital asset. Learn more about
managing such an asset at Acquire to dispose - introduction to the end-to-end
business process.

Description:
Project contracts serve as a legally binding agreement between a project
provider and a client in the project sales process. It outlines the scope,
deliverables, timelines, costs, and terms of the project. This document ensures
both parties' expectations are aligned, mitigates potential conflicts, and
provides a framework for successful project execution. It acts as a safeguard,
promoting transparency and accountability throughout the project's lifecycle.




Effective project contract management faces multifaceted challenges. Navigating
complex legal frameworks, ensuring compliance with evolving regulations, and
managing diverse stakeholder expectations strains seamless execution.
Ambiguities in contract terms and obligations often lead to disputes, demanding
meticulous communication and documentation. Integrating digital tools for
efficient tracking while fostering clear vendor-client collaboration remains
vital. Addressing these challenges fosters successful project delivery,
minimizing risks and optimizing outcomes.



Modern trends in project contract management include a shift towards
digitalization and automation, with the integration of contract lifecycle
management (CLM) software. The adoption of AI-powered tools for contract
analysis and risk assessment, increased emphasis on data security and privacy
compliance within contracts, growing integration of blockchain for transparent
and tamper-proof contract records, and the utilization of collaborative cloud
platforms for real-time updates and communication. These trends aim to enhance
efficiency, accuracy, and collaboration while mitigating legal and operational
risks in project contract management.



In conclusion, the project contract stands as the cornerstone of the project
sales process, encapsulating terms, deliverables, timelines, and expectations.
It safeguards interests, ensuring a clear understanding between parties. Its
meticulous formulation cultivates trust, minimizes disputes, and paves the way
for successful project execution, fostering enduring client relationships.

that your project is profitable according to the baseline.

The manage project delivery business process area is key to tracking the work
that is delivered on a project. It helps ensure that the final outcomes are
provided to stakeholders in a diligent and timely manner. During this phase, all
the tasks, activities, and milestones that are outlined in the project plan are
performed and completed. Depending on the nature of the project, work might
include various activities, such as the examples in the following list:

 * Design
 * Development
 * Testing
 * Documentation
 * Quality assurance

We recommend that you use a structured approach to track, record, and manage the
effort that team members and resources invest in these activities. In this way,
you gain valuable insights into how the project is progressing and how project
objectives are being met.



This business process area also covers the evaluation of project performance,
estimation of task completion times, and identification of potential
bottlenecks. In addition, it facilitates the assessment of resource allocation,
and therefore helps optimize workforce utilization and enhance project
efficiency. Through the systematic capture of project time, organizations
enhance their ability to deliver projects on schedule, allocate resources
effectively, and boost overall productivity.



Ideally, the structure of the manage project delivery business process is
defined during the early stages of project implementation. By outlining the
manage project delivery process as project parameters, timelines, and resource
allocation are being established, you ensure that accurate data collection
begins from the project's inception. Although the process might naturally evolve
as the project progresses, it's important to lay its foundation before the
project work begins.

Description:
The monitor and analyze project performance business process area focuses on
systematically monitoring, assessing, and evaluating various project elements,
including the following list:

 * How much of the project scope is already delivered?
 * What remains?
 * What are the project costs and revenue?
 * Are there any risks?
 * Which issues prevent the project from progressing as planned and meeting its
   objectives?

By monitoring project performance and conducting in-depth analysis, project
managers and stakeholders can gain valuable insights, make informed decisions,
and take any corrective action that is required.



The process of monitoring and analyzing project performance should be
established at the onset of the project. As soon as the project objectives,
scope, and resources are defined, it's imperative to set up a monitoring and
analysis mechanism. In this way, you ensure that a system for gauging progress,
measuring performance, and implementing course corrections is in place from the
earliest stages. Early incorporation of this business process area also ensures
that data collection is consistent throughout the project, so that insights for
analysis are more accurate.

Description:
The prospect to quote business process flow is a sales process that starts with
identifying potential customers (prospects). It ends with providing prospects
with a quote for the product or service they're interested in purchasing. The
following stages fit into this process:




 1. Define sales strategy: This overarching step guides the overall sales
    process, including the prospect-to-quote stage. It involves setting goals,
    defining target markets, and creating a plan to achieve sales objectives.
 2. Run marketing campaigns: Marketing campaigns play a role in lead generation
    and help attract potential customers. This step can be considered part of
    the lead generation process within the prospect-to-quote stage.
    
 3. Identify and qualify leads: This step is essential in the prospect-to-quote
    process, as it involves finding potential customers and assessing their fit
    and potential value to the organization.
    
 4. Pursue opportunities: This step aligns with the initial contact, needs
    assessment, and solution development stages in the prospect-to-quote
    process. It involves engaging with prospects and working to create tailored
    solutions that meet their needs.
    
 5. Estimate and quote sales: This step corresponds to the proposal creation and
    presentation stages. It involves creating and presenting a detailed quote or
    proposal to the prospect.
    
 6. Manage customer relationships: While customer relationship management is an
    ongoing activity throughout the sales cycle, it plays a role in the
    prospect-to-quote process, particularly in the follow-up, negotiation, and
    quote revision stages.

Every organization has some variation of the prospect to quote end-to-end
scenario. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization that is looking
to implement a technology solution to support the prospect to quote business
process.

Description: Relation types classify the business relationship represented by a prospect. Sales and marketing administrators establish the available values before prospect creation so each new prospect can be identified consistently, with common concepts including customer, vendor, new, imported, qualified, or not qualified. The default relation type in Sales and marketing parameters can be proposed when a prospect is created, but users should still understand when another type is appropriate. Title 6: Review line of business in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description: Line of business codes classify customers or vendors by an industry or economic-activity grouping in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Master-data administrators create a code and description for each approved classification, then apply it consistently where business partners must be analyzed by sector. The organization may align values with an external standard or use an internal structure, but the governing source, level of detail, and ownership should be explicit. Avoid parallel codes for the same industry, ambiguous abbreviations, and changes that make historical reporting misleading. Coordinate assignments with customer and vendor onboarding, segmentation, compliance, and reporting processes. Validate representative organizations and confirm that users can distinguish neighboring classifications without relying on informal knowledge. Questions to ask include which external or internal standard governs sector reporting, how organizations with several activities are classified, and who approves reclassification. Listen for indicators such as different codes for the same industry, missing classifications, acquisitions changing a partner's primary activity, regulatory reporting needs, or mappings maintained separately in spreadsheets. Title 6: Review statistics group in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description: Statistics groups define reusable customer classifications for inquiries, reports, and sales analysis in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Sales or master-data administrators create a group code and description for each stable population that the organization needs to compare, then assign the appropriate group to customer records. Design groups around a clear analytical purpose rather than duplicating geography, customer group, line of business, or another existing attribute. Use mutually understandable names, document ownership, and establish how new customers are classified and how exceptions are corrected. Preserve historical interpretation when a group is retired or reorganized, because changing its meaning can distort trends. Validate representative customers and confirm the group produces the intended inquiry or report population. Questions to ask include which customer populations management compares, how assignment decisions are made, and who monitors completeness. Title 6: Create and configure responsibilities in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description: Responsibilities define the sales-management roles that can be associated with business records and activities in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Sales administrators create a responsibility with a clear business meaning, then identify where it is applicable, including contexts such as customers, prospects, leads, opportunities, campaigns, call lists, cases, vendors, or sales units. This lets teams describe who contributes to a relationship or selling process without relying only on job titles or free text. Keep the list aligned with actual accountability, distinguish responsibilities that drive different reporting or ownership decisions, and avoid duplicates that merely use alternate wording. Validate each value on representative records and confirm that users understand when to select it. Questions to ask include which forms of accountability must be visible across the sales lifecycle, where responsibilities differ from formal positions, and who maintains changes. Listen for indicators such as unclear account ownership, responsibilities tracked in notes, duplicate role labels, inconsistent use across record types, or reporting that cannot explain who contributed to an outcome. Owner mapping requires review before publication.

Title 6: Create and configure source types in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
Description: Source types classify how leads and opportunities originate in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Sales and marketing administrators create a source type and description for each stable acquisition channel or referral category the organization needs to analyze, then maintain the available options associated with that type. The design should distinguish meaningful origins such as campaigns, events, partner referrals, web inquiries, or other approved channels without creating a new value for every individual activity. Use names that salespeople can select consistently, define ownership for changes, and align the classifications with campaign and pipeline reporting. Retire obsolete options carefully so historical records remain interpretable. Validate the values on representative leads and opportunities and confirm that reports group them as intended. Questions to ask include which acquisition channels influence investment decisions, how source information is captured before sales accepts a lead, and who resolves ambiguous origins. Listen for indicators such as free-text sources, duplicate channels, excessive use of an unknown value, missing partner attribution, or campaign results that cannot be reconciled with opportunities. Owner mapping requires review before publication.

Quotation template groups organize reusable sales quotation templates so users can find and apply the appropriate starting content when preparing quotations. A group is a prerequisite for creating quotation templates and provides a stable category for managing related offers.

Create a concise identifier and description for each meaningful template family before defining the templates themselves. Decide whether groups represent product lines, customer segments, campaign offers, regions, or another durable business distinction. Assign ownership for group and template maintenance, avoid overlapping categories, and retire unused groups without changing the historical meaning of quotations created from their templates.

Template groups are consumed when quotation templates are created and when users select reusable content for individual or mass sales quotations. Validate a group by creating a representative template within it and applying that template to a quotation, confirming that users can locate the correct family and obtain the expected lines or terms. Review groups when offerings, sales channels, quotation policy, or template ownership changes. Owner mapping requires review before publication.

Description:
The record to report (R2R) process is sometimes referred to as the financial
recording and close process. It's a critical end-to-end business process that
the finance and accounting department of an organization typically owns. The R2R
process involves the collection, analysis, and reporting of financial data to
make sure that the company's financial statements accurately reflect its
financial performance.

The R2R process typically includes several key sub-processes such as:

 * Data gathering:
   
   This process involves the collection of financial data from various sources
   such as accounts payable, accounts receivable, and general ledger. Dynamics
   365 Finance is a double-entry, near-real time, accounting system that
   automatically posts all transactions from other modules such as sales,
   purchases, and production to a sub-ledger and to the general ledger
   simultaneously.

 * Journal entry:
   
   This process involves the recording of financial transactions in the
   company's general ledger. In Dynamics 365 Finance, the process uses general
   journals. Other types of journals are available in other modules such as
   Accounts payable and Accounts receivable to post invoices and payments, for
   example. These journals automatically post to the general ledger without
   other manual user interaction.

 * Account reconciliation:
   
   This process involves the comparison of financial data from different sources
   to ensure that they're consistent and accurate. Dynamics 365 Finance includes
   various tools and reports to help support the process of account
   reconciliation such as the financial period close workspace.

 * Financial reporting:
   
   This process involves the preparation of financial statements such as the
   balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement. Use Dynamics 365
   Finance together with Power BI, Azure Data Lakes, or Financial Reporter to
   quickly and easily manage and create financial reports and statements for
   your organization.

 * Financial analysis:
   
   This process involves the interpretation of financial data to identify
   trends, patterns, and anomalies.

Overall, the R2R process is a critical business process that helps organizations
make sure of the accuracy and completeness of their financial statements. It's
essential for making informed business decisions and meeting regulatory
requirements.

Important: The process defined here does not include other business processes
such as procure to pay, order to cash, plan to produce, and payroll processing,
which are typically performed by other departments such as procurement, sales,
manufacturing, and human resources. For more information about these processes,
see Order to cash introduction, Procure to pay introduction, Plan to produce
introduction, and Hire to retire introduction.

Every organization has variations to the record to report process. Here, we
define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology
solution to support the record to report.

Description:
In a Dynamics 365 implementation, definition of the financial structure and
definition of organizational policies are crucial steps that significantly
affect the success of the implementation and the overall efficiency of the
business processes. In Dynamics 365 Finance, the chart of accounts, financial
dimensions, and many General ledger parameters and configurations are used in
downstream processes. Because Dynamics 365 Finance is a double-entry system that
integrates directly with Dynamics 365 Commerce, Project Operations, and Supply
Chain Management, all entries that are posted to a subledger are also posted to
the general ledger.



By defining the financial structure early and clearly in your implementation,
you help ensure accurate financial reporting, compliance, data consistency, and
cost allocations. The financial structure in a Dynamics 365 Finance
implementation includes the chart of accounts, cost centers, profit centers,
financial reporting structures, tax codes, and more.



Organizational accounting policies include things such as the legal entity or
company structure, elimination and consolidation rules, and intercompany
accounting configuration, including centralized payments. They also define how
you handle currency conversion and revaluation of your financial data throughout
the system. In addition, if you use the Fixed assets or Asset leasing module, it
covers the asset-related company policies. If you use the Cash and bank
management module, it covers the banking policies and configurations. It's
important to design your processes so that they are streamlined and efficient,
to help reduce manual intervention and minimize errors. When you define your
organizational accounting policies, you should consider standardizing them
across companies and departments. By implementing consistent business processes
across the organization, you help ensure uniformity and reduce confusion among
employees. This standardization is especially important when different
geographies, departments, or companies are involved. Although Dynamics 365
Finance supports flexible configuration across legal entities, the more
processes you can standardize, the smoother your implementation is.



Many other areas rely on or are affected by the decisions that are made in the
define financial structure and organizational accounting policies area.
Therefore, the business processes in this area should be defined as early as
possible in the overall implementation project.

Title 6: Create and configure financial dimension in Dynamics 365 Finance
Description:
Financial dimensions define the business attributes used with main accounts to classify transactions for management, statutory, operational, and analytical reporting. A dimension must be created and activated before it can participate in account structures or be consumed on transactions.

Select the appropriate source for each dimension, establish a clear name and ownership model, and review the available dimension values before activation. Coordinate the design with account structures, advanced rules, default dimensions, value security, hierarchies, translations, and integrations. Use Activate all only after the complete design has been reviewed, because activation updates the dimension framework and makes the dimensions available to dependent configuration. Avoid dimensions that duplicate information already represented by another governed attribute.

Activated dimensions are consumed across journals, subledgers, budgets, projects, assets, allocations, and reporting. Validate by adding the dimension to an account structure, posting representative combinations, and confirming inquiry and report results. Questions to ask include which business decisions require separate analysis, where values originate, and who owns their lifecycle. Listen for indicators such as dimensions created only to fix one report, uncontrolled value lists, duplicate analytical meanings, or posting combinations that users cannot interpret.

Access this configuration from multiple menu locations, including General Ledger > Chart of accounts > Dimensions > Financial dimensions; General ledger > Chart of accounts > Dimensions > Financial dimensions. Title 5: Define daily exchange rates in Dynamics 365 Finance
Description:
Daily rates are used to convert foreign currency transactions into the
accounting currency for specific dates. These rates ensure that transactions are
recorded accurately based on the exchange rate applicable to the specific day of
the transaction, providing a precise reflection of the value of foreign currency
transactions. by using daily rates, companies can maintain accurate financial

Title 6: Create and maintain sales tax settlement period in Dynamics 365 Finance
Description:
Create, review, update, or remove sales tax settlement period setup using the captured Sales tax settlement periods page. Sales tax settlement periods define the filing and payment intervals over which posted sales tax is collected for settlement with a tax authority. Each legal-entity record identifies the authority, interval frequency and duration, payment terms, correction treatment, and the dated periods available for settlement.

Before configuration, establish the sales tax authority and agree the statutory filing calendar, payment timing, correction policy, and whether settlement should use batch processing. Create the period intervals that cover the required reporting dates without gaps or unintended overlap. Coordinate the design with sales tax codes, because each code references a settlement period and will be settled according to that calendar.

The period is consumed by sales tax settlement and payment processing and supports inquiries into posted tax and settlements by interval. Validate it by assigning a representative tax code, posting transactions within a defined interval, and running a controlled settlement to confirm the date range, authority, corrections, and payment result. Review periods before each new reporting year and whenever authorities or filing frequencies change, because missing or incorrect intervals can delay settlement or include transactions in the wrong return.

Description:
Budget management is a cornerstone of financial planning and control, and holds
profound significance for businesses across industries. It empowers
organizations to allocate resources efficiently, make informed financial
decisions, and chart a course towards sustainable growth. In an era marked by
economic volatility and shifting market dynamics, a robust budget management
strategy underpins not only fiscal responsibility but also the ability to adapt
and thrive in changing circumstances. By leveraging Dynamics 365 to streamline
this critical business process, enterprises can harness the power of data-driven
insights, automation, and real-time visibility, ultimately optimizing their
financial performance and enhancing their competitive edge.



The budgeting features of Dynamics 365 Finance can be added at any point in your
project or post go-live; however, we recommend that you consider including the
basic budgeting features in your project at a minimum to harness the full
flexibility and data visibility into budgets versus actuals. If Dynamics 365
Finance is not your system of record for financials, we recommend that you
integrate your actual or the totals of your financial transactions into your
system of record for financials where you do manage your budget. As part of a
holistic ERP implementation, budget management should be integrated into your
organization's operations, enabling real-time insights, collaboration, and
data-driven decision-making.

Description:
Efficiently recording financial transactions is a cornerstone of organizational
success, serving as the bedrock for informed decision-making, compliance, and
financial stability. In the realm of Dynamics 365, this process gains an extra
layer of precision and agility, transforming the way businesses handle their
financial data. The significance of recording financial transactions lies in its
ability to provide a real-time, accurate snapshot of an organization's fiscal
health. Dynamics 365 Finance and Business Central enhance this importance by
streamlining the entire transaction recording process, offering robust tools and
features that contribute to better financial management.



Implementing Dynamics 365 Finance involves navigating a series of crucial
business processes to ensure seamless financial transaction recording. The
overall processes include defining policies, setting approval workflows,
managing ledger postings, recording entries, correcting vouchers, handling
accruals, managing deferrals, and processing allocations. These steps
collectively ensure accurate, real-time financial data. In a Dynamics 365
implementation, start with clear policies and early approval workflows,
progressively addressing ledger management, journal entries, and voucher
corrections. Strategic integration of accruals, deferrals, and allocations at
different project stages maximizes the system's potential, optimizing financial
transaction recording.



When embarking on a Dynamics 365 Finance implementation, addressing the
aforementioned processes strategically is paramount. Begin by defining clear
policies and procedures, setting the stage for a robust financial transaction
recording system. Early in the project, establish the approval process for
journals to ensure a streamlined workflow. As the implementation progresses,
focus on managing ledger postings, recording journal entries, and correcting
vouchers. Accruals, deferrals, and allocations should be methodically integrated
into the system to enhance the accuracy and completeness of financial data. By
approaching these processes thoughtfully at different stages of the project,
organizations can unlock the full potential of Dynamics 365 Finance in
revolutionizing their financial transaction recording practices.

Title 5: Manually record journal entries in Dynamics 365 Finance
Description:
Manually recording journal entries are used to record financial transactions
directly in General Ledger. These manual entries can include transactions that
are not automatically posted by the system, such as adjusting entries, accruals,
or other entries that require direct input.  Manually recording journal entries
is a straightforward process that requires selecting the correct journal type,
entering debit and credit lines, validating the entry, and then posting it to
the General Ledger, By following these steps, you ensure accurate financial
reporting and maintain proper internal controls for your organization's
financial transactions. Things to consider while recording manual journal

organizations streamline their service delivery and invoicing processes. It
enables businesses to manage their customer service interactions and turn them
into revenue-generating opportunities.

create service agreements with customers, manage their resources, track their
time and expenses, and generate invoices for services rendered. This automation
helps them reduce manual effort, minimize errors, and improve billing accuracy.

   service requests, manage their schedules, and track their time and expenses.
 * Invoicing: Enables organizations to generate invoices based on service
   agreements and track payments.
 * Analytics: Provides insights into service performance and profitability to
   help organizations make informed decisions.

Overall, service to cash for Dynamics 365 can help organizations improve their
service delivery, increase customer satisfaction, and generate more revenue.

define the basic outline for any organization that is looking to implement a

Administer to operate serves as the linchpin for the sustained success of
Dynamics 365 within organizational landscapes. Focused on the ongoing
administration and optimization of existing solutions, this end-to-end business
process entails a comprehensive approach to ensure the seamless operation of
Dynamics 365. It's important to note that administer to operate primarily
concentrates on post-implementation processes, with the Dynamics 365
Implementation Guide serving as a dedicated resource for initial deployment and
installation guidance.




Within the administer to operate framework, various critical processes are
orchestrated to maintain the health and efficiency of Dynamics 365 solutions.
Encompassing a range of critical processes, this end-to-end business process
involves defining business continuity plans, managing licensing and
entitlements, administering system features, ensuring system access and
security, training users for increased adoption, monitoring systems and
capacity, managing background jobs and notifications, adopting software
releases, overseeing data synchronization, ensuring system compliance, and
providing responsive support.



While primarily addressing post-implementation needs, administer to operate
plays a pivotal role in maintaining the efficiency, compliance, and adaptability
of Dynamics 365 solutions, ensuring they continually align with evolving
business processes and user requirements. For initial deployment and
installation guidance, organizations can refer to the Dynamics 365
Implementation Guide, recognizing administer to operate as the cornerstone for
ongoing optimization and resilience.



In summary, administer to operate encompasses a multifaceted approach to
sustainably manage, optimize, and support Dynamics 365 solutions throughout
their lifecycle, ensuring they remain aligned with organizational goals and
responsive to evolving business dynamics.



Every organization has variations to the administer to operate processes. Here,
we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a
technology solution to support the administer to operate process with Dynamics
365.
